baseline.searchScope: Both full pinned Mathlib/Mathlib and TauCeti/TauCeti trees, with targeted Pfister, Henselization, biinterpretability, Kronecker-dimension, patch, normalization, valuation-place, high-degree pole, approximation and cohomology searches. Absence of an exact hit is recorded as an audit result, not a theorem about every possible library encoding.

conventions: Fields are finitely generated as fields over their prime field, not necessarily as rings. Additive valuations satisfy v(0)=infinity and O_v={x:v(x)>=0}; equivalent valuations are identified.
H_d means d>=3, K finitely generated of Kronecker dimension d, and, only if char K=2 and d>3, resolution of singularities above F_2 in the two-part sense recorded below.

All Pfister parameters are nonzero. In characteristic two the first factors are bilinear and the last is the nonsingular quadratic binary form x^2+xy+a_0 y^2. Non-dyadic excludes mixed characteristic (0,2), not equal characteristic two.
An interpretation may use a finite tuple of parameters. The concluding sentence is parameter-free. Uniformity is for each fixed dimension, not a single formula for all dimensions.

items.name: Geometric and arithmetic prime divisors
items.statement: For F of finite Kronecker dimension a prime divisor is a nontrivial discrete valuation w with dim_Kr(Fw)=dim_Kr(F)-1, taken up to equivalence. It is geometric if char(Fw)=char(F), and arithmetic otherwise.

api.name: DittmannPop.primeDivisor.compatibility

items.name: Residue-dimension characterization of prime divisors
items.statement: Let K be a finitely generated field and v any valuation with dim_Kr(Kv)=dim_Kr(K)−1. Then the valuation ring is a DVR and Kv is finitely generated over its prime field. Thus v is a prime divisor in the paper’s sense. The proof covers geometric and arithmetic valuations and does not assume discreteness in advance.
items.note: The exact criterion has a direct proof in both characteristic cases. Finite generation of K is essential: Fp(t^{1/p^∞}) has residue Fp and transcendence degree 1 but value group Z[1/p], which is not discrete. No new full reading of Engler–Prestel is claimed.
proofSteps: The valuation cannot be trivial because a trivial valuation has residue field K and preserves its Kronecker dimension.

In equal characteristic, geometric-gauss-subfield exhibits K as a one-variable function field over the subfield generated by residue-basis lifts. Its proper valuation subring contains that base, so import the already built function-field-discreteness theorem. Alternatively its restriction to F0 has cyclic value group, and the same finite-extension argument as below applies.

In mixed characteristic, the Kronecker-dimension equality is precisely trdeg_Fp(Kv)=trdeg_Q(K). Arithmetic-gauss-subfield gives a finite subextension F0=Q(x) with cyclic value group generated by v(p).

The general valuation-extension-ef theorem gives finite index of the base value group and finite degree of the residue extension in either case. Finite-index-cyclic-value and the pinned cyclic-value-dvr theorem give a DVR without assuming it.

The residue field of F0 is a finitely generated rational field over the residue prime field. Its finite residue extension Kv is therefore finitely generated. This supplies both discreteness and residue finite generation at the required scope.

Parameters are allowed and tracked. Equivalently pullbacks of every B-definable finite-power set are A-definable.

items.name: Finitely generated fields and integer arithmetic
items.statement: Every infinite finitely generated field K is parametrically bi-interpretable with (Z,+,×). Assume resolution above F_2 only when char K=2 and dim_Kr(K)>3.
proofSteps: Use low-dimensional-biinterpretability when dim_Kr(K)<=2.
In H_d with d>=3, construct the definable normalization R_T and its fraction-pair bi-interpretation with K.
Apply AKNS Theorem 3.1 to the infinite finitely generated R_T and compose bi-interpretations.

items.name: Single field axiom
items.statement: For each finitely generated field K, subject to resolution above F_2 if char K=2 and dim_Kr(K)>3, there exists a parameter-free sentence θ_K in the ring language such that every finitely generated FIELD L satisfies θ_K exactly when L≅K.
proofSteps: For finite K use the exact-cardinality field sentence.
For infinite K, use main-biinterpretability and the total-inversion language bridge before applying the finite-language QFA theorem.

items.name: Finite-field base case
items.statement: For a finite field K of size q=p^n, the ring sentence saying characteristic p and exactly q elements characterizes K up to field isomorphism among fields. No bi-interpretation with Z is asserted for a finite field.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, finite case; §1 reduction to infinite fields
items.note: Elementary expansion of the finite case, not a claim of an effective uniform formula in q.
proofSteps: Assert exactly q elements with q existential witnesses, pairwise distinctness and a universal exhaustion clause.
Add characteristic p if desired; uniqueness of finite fields gives the isomorphism type among fields.

items.name: Torsion Tate coefficient complex
items.statement: For n>0, Z/n(i)=μ_n^{⊗i} if char F does not divide n. If char F=p and n=mp^r with p∤m, use μ_m^{⊗i}⊕W_rΩ^i_log[-i] on the étale site. Hence H^j(F,Z/n(i)) has wild summand H^{j-i}(F,W_rΩ^i_log). The paper uses n=2 and i>=0.

items.name: Discrete valuation residue
items.statement: In the coefficient/valuation regimes used in Facts 2.1–2.3, a discrete valuation w of F has a boundary ∂_w:H^{i+1}(F)→H^i(Fw), factoring through restriction to the w-henselization. In mixed residue characteristic two the required hypotheses must be supplied separately; no unrestricted residue map is inferred.

api.name: DittmannPop.cohomologyResidue.structure

api.name: DittmannPop.cohomologyResidue.compatibility

items.name: Characters and Brauer torsion
items.statement: For every field F and n>0 with the Kato coefficient convention, H^1(F,Z/n(0))=Hom_cont(G_F,Z/n), and H^2(F,Z/n(1))=Br(F)[n]. The characteristic-dividing case uses logarithmic coefficients.
proofSteps: Use the constant étale coefficient in degree zero for H¹.
Use the Kummer sequence away from the characteristic and the logarithmic Kato coefficient comparison in the wild case for H².
The latter comparison is not implied by the triviality of μ_p-points.

items.name: Fields obtained from global constant places
items.statement: For a relatively algebraically closed global subfield k_1⊂K and a place v of k_1, take k_{1v} to be its henselization at finite v, its real closure at real v, and its algebraic closure at complex v inside the completion. Let K_v=Kk_{1v}, embedded in the corresponding function field over the completion. Keep henselian and completed fields distinct.
items.note: The PDF's displayed tensor defining the completed compositum has a notation mismatch; the original Jannsen formulation uses completed base change.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.constantPlaceFields.characterise
api.statement: At finite v the algebraic local base is the henselization.

api.name: DittmannPop.constantPlaceFields.structure
api.statement: At real v the algebraic local base is the specified real closure.

api.name: DittmannPop.constantPlaceFields.compatibility
api.statement: Restriction to completion-base function fields factors through K_v.

tests.statement: For the real place of Q, k_{1v} is real algebraic, not all of R.

tests.name: DittmannPop.constantPlaceFields.test2

tests.name: DittmannPop.constantPlaceFields.test3

items.name: Jannsen local–global injectivity over a global base
items.statement: Let K be finitely generated of Kronecker dimension d>=1, char K≠2, and k_1⊂K a relatively algebraically closed global subfield. Then α∈H^{d+1}(K) is zero iff its restrictions to H^{d+1}(K_v) vanish for every place v of k_1.
items.locator: Fact 2.1; Jannsen Theorem 0.4, with transcendence dimension d−1
items.note: Original theorem statement checked in published Jannsen pp.2–3; full 71-page proof not claimed read.
proofSteps: Apply Jannsen Theorem 0.4 to completed global-base function fields.
Relate the henselian/real algebraic base changes to the completions in the permitted setting; injectivity of the required map is a distinct comparison input.
The original higher Hasse proof and this comparison still need full dependency auditing.

items.name: Arithmetic Bloch–Ogus complex
items.statement: For the excellent normal integral d-dimensional schemes in Facts 2.2–2.3, form the homological complex with degree a term ⊕_{x:dim closure{x}=a}H^{a+1}(κ(x)); its top term is H^{d+1}(κ(X)) and top differential is the sum of codimension-one residues. The residue differentials satisfy d²=0.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.katoComplex.characterise
api.statement: Its degree-a term is the direct sum of H^{a+1}(κ(x)) over dimension-a points.

api.name: DittmannPop.katoComplex.structure
api.statement: Its top term is H^{d+1} of the function field.

api.name: DittmannPop.katoComplex.compatibility
api.statement: Consecutive residue differentials compose to zero.

tests.name: DittmannPop.katoComplex.test1
tests.statement: For a curve the terms are H^2(K) and the sum of H^1 of closed-point residues.

tests.name: DittmannPop.katoComplex.test2
tests.statement: For a zero-dimensional field model only the H^1 term remains.

tests.name: DittmannPop.katoComplex.test3
tests.statement: The boundary composite is zero, not an arbitrary family of unrelated maps.

items.name: Kerz–Saito divisorial detection
items.statement: Let R be a finite field of characteristic≠2, or the henselian valuation ring of a global field at a finite place with residue characteristic≠2. For X proper, regular, integral, flat over R of positive dimension d, and K=κ(X), α∈H^{d+1}(K) vanishes iff its restrictions to the henselizations at all codimension-one points vanish.
items.note: R is not assumed an arbitrary valuation ring; theorem 8.1 statement and its reduction proof read, prerequisite theorem proofs remain open.
proofSteps: Apply Kerz–Saito Theorem 8.1 to the proper regular model with invertible coefficient 2.
Top-degree exactness in the Kato complex detects a class by codimension-one residues.
Residues factor through the corresponding henselizations; global zero clearly restricts to zero.

items.name: Divisorial detection in characteristic two
items.statement: Let K be finitely generated of characteristic two and Kronecker dimension d>0; for d>3 assume resolution above F_2. On a projective smooth F_2-model X of K, α∈H^{d+1}(K) vanishes iff its restrictions to the henselizations at all x∈X^(1) vanish.
items.locator: Fact 2.3; Jannsen Theorem 0.10; Kato/Suwa in low dimension
items.note: The low-dimensional unconditional input and existence of the indicated model are distinct proof obligations.
proofSteps: Use the smooth projective model supplied in the applicable dimension/resolution regime.
Apply the wild Kato-complex Hasse principle, combining the Jannsen finite-field result with Suwa's logarithmic comparison.
Record Cossart–Piltant and the low-dimensional arguments separately; no general characteristic-two resolution theorem is claimed.

items.name: Odd-degree persistence of mod-two classes
items.statement: If E/F is a finite extension of odd degree and char F is different from 2, restriction H^m(F,Z/2(i))→H^m(E,Z/2(i)) is injective for every nonnegative degree m and twist i used here. Separability is not required.
proofSteps: Factor E/F as a finite separable extension E_s/F followed by a purely inseparable extension E/E_s. Both degrees are odd.
For the separable part, corestriction composed with restriction is multiplication by [E_s:F], hence identity on mod-two cohomology.

For the purely inseparable part, Spec E→Spec E_s is a universal homeomorphism. The equivalence of small etale sites preserves mu_2 and its twists and gives an isomorphism on the cohomology groups (Stacks 04DY, Theorem 59.45.2 and Proposition 59.45.4). Compose the two maps.

items.name: Prime-to-two regular alteration
items.statement: Let R be an excellent henselian DVR with residue characteristic different from 2, S=Spec R, and X an integral projective flat S-scheme with nonempty generic fibre. There is a finite odd-degree extension eta_prime/Frac(R), with S_prime the normalization of S in eta_prime, and a projective dominant generically finite alteration h:Y→X of odd function-field degree, where Y is regular integral and quasi-projective over S_prime. For this projective X, Y is projective over S and over S_prime. No separability of either finite extension is asserted.
items.locator: Proposition 3.4, p.8; supplier ILO Exposé X, Theorem 2.4 and proof 2.6, printed pp.152–155 (arXiv:1207.3648 PDF pp.158–161)
items.note: de Jong arbitrary-degree alterations do not imply this prime-to-two statement. Original theorem and proof are acquisition gaps.
proofSteps: Apply ILO X.2.4 with l=2 and empty boundary. Spec R is separated, integral, noetherian, excellent, regular, one-dimensional, and 2 is invertible.

Take the dominating regular integral component if needed; the l-prime alteration definition controls its function-field degree. Normalize the base in the permitted odd-degree extension. Projectivity over S follows from h and X; properness plus quasi-projectivity over S_prime gives projectivity there.

A regular integral model dominating the trait is flat. The finite local base remains the henselian valuation ring of a finite extension of the global field at a finite place, so the model local-global theorem applies.

Use odd-degree-injectivity, including its purely inseparable comparison, rather than silently imposing separability on the alteration. The complete Gabber/Vidal/log-modification proof chain is a supplier blueprint task.

items.name: Pfister form with two invertible
items.statement: For a field F with char F≠2 and nonzero a_i,…,a_0, q_a is the tensor product of the diagonal binary forms ⟨1,−a_j⟩ for j=i,…,0; it has dimension 2^{i+1}.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.pfisterOdd.structure

api.name: DittmannPop.pfisterOdd.compatibility

items.name: Pfister isotropy and hyperbolicity
items.statement: In either characteristic convention, a positive-fold quadratic Pfister form q_a is isotropic iff it is hyperbolic. In characteristic≠2 this exceeds the upstream result restricted to at most two folds.
proofSteps: Use roundness and EKM Proposition 9.8(2) to remove one binary outer factor.
For a single nonsingular binary factor, an isotropic vector gives a hyperbolic plane.
Induct on the fold number, in both characteristic conventions.

items.name: Cohomological symbol of a Pfister form
items.statement: An (i+1)-fold quadratic Pfister form q_a has its canonical symbol invariant e(q_a)∈H^{i+1}(F,Z/2(i)): the usual mod-two Kummer symbol away from characteristic two and the characteristic-two quadratic/logarithmic invariant in EKM§16. Its normalization uses q=x²+xy+a_0y² in characteristic two.
items.note: The characteristic-two comparison is a separate theorem; do not substitute μ_2.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.pfisterInvariant.characterise
api.statement: An n-fold form has invariant in H^n(F,Z/2(n−1)).

api.name: DittmannPop.pfisterInvariant.structure

api.name: DittmannPop.pfisterInvariant.compatibility

tests.name: DittmannPop.pfisterInvariant.test3

items.name: Vanishing of the Pfister symbol
items.statement: q_a is isotropic over F iff e(q_a)=0 in H^{i+1}(F). The proof uses the symbol comparison and the Arason–Pfister dimension criterion, not merely a formal norm-residue isomorphism.
items.note: Original EKM proofs remain to be acquired.
proofSteps: The zero invariant places the Witt class in I_q^{n+1}.
Its anisotropic part has dimension at most 2^n; the Arason–Pfister bound forces it to be zero.
Hyperbolic Pfister forms are isotropic, and conversely have zero invariant.

items.name: Naturality of the Pfister symbol
items.statement: For every field extension E/F, e((q_a)_E)=res_E/F(e(q_a)).
proofSteps: Check the symbol's Kummer or Artin–Schreier/logarithmic construction commutes with field extension.
Transport this through the relevant cohomological comparison.

items.name: Henselization of an arbitrary valued field
items.statement: For a valuation w of F, the w-henselization F_w is a separable algebraic immediate extension with its canonical extended henselian valuation, initial among compatible henselian valued extensions. Higher-rank valuations are permitted.
items.note: No pinned arbitrary-valuation henselization construction found; p-adic Hensel lemmas are narrower.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.henselization.characterise
api.statement: The canonical field embedding respects the valuation.

api.name: DittmannPop.henselization.structure
api.statement: It extends uniquely to compatible henselian valued targets.

api.name: DittmannPop.henselization.compatibility
api.statement: Its residue-field and value-group maps are isomorphisms.

tests.statement: Henselizing an already henselian field changes it only by canonical valued isomorphism.

tests.name: DittmannPop.henselization.test2

tests.name: DittmannPop.henselization.test3

items.name: Unit Pfister isotropy and residue isotropy
items.statement: Let (F,w) be nontrivially henselian and non-dyadic, and all entries ε_j of a Pfister form be w-units. Then q_ε is isotropic over F iff its residue form is isotropic over Fw. Smoothness of the unit quadric and Hensel lifting give one direction; reduction of a minimally valued coordinate gives the other.
proofSteps: A nonzero residue zero of the nonsingular unit quadric lifts by Hensel's lemma.
For the converse scale a nonzero isotropic vector so a coordinate is a unit and all coordinates are integral; reduce it.
For arbitrary value groups choose a coordinate of minimal value among the finite set.

items.name: Principal-unit Pfister factor
items.statement: Under the preceding non-dyadic henselian unit hypotheses, if w(ε_1−1)>0 then q_{ε_1,ε_0} is isotropic, and so is any Pfister form having it as a factor.
proofSteps: Its residue outer parameter is 1, so the residue binary-factor extension is hyperbolic.
Lift residue isotropy by unit-reduction-isotropy and then retain the zero vector in the larger tensor form.

items.name: Independent valuation classes and anisotropy
items.statement: In a non-dyadic henselian field (F,w), let ε be a unit tuple and π_s,…,π_1∈F× have linearly independent images in wF/2wF. Then residue isotropy of q_ε, isotropy of q_ε over F, and isotropy of q_{π,ε} over F are equivalent.
items.note: In odd characteristic the tensor expansion carries (−1)^{|χ|}; these signs have value zero and do not change the distinct-value proof. Each block has N+1 coordinates; see E10.
proofSteps: Expand into blocks weighted by products of the π_i.
Distinct mod-two value classes prevent cancellation among minimal-value anisotropic blocks.
The reverse direction extends an isotropic vector through one tensor summand.

items.name: Kronecker dimension drops under a valuation
items.statement: For any field F of finite Kronecker dimension and any nontrivial valuation v, dim_Kr(Fv)<dim_Kr(F). No finite-generation, rank-one, discreteness or henselianity hypothesis is required. The direct residue-lifting proof separates equal and mixed characteristic and does not require the full Abhyankar inequality.
items.note: The exact dimension-drop input is now proved mathematically below. The general Engler–Prestel theorem is not claimed as newly read or formalized.
proofSteps: If F and Fv have the same characteristic, the valuation is trivial on the prime field. Lift any finite residue-independent tuple and adjoin one element of positive value. The lifting lemma makes this enlarged tuple algebraically independent in F, so trdeg(Fv)+1≤trdeg(F). The two Kronecker dimensions have the same characteristic offset.

If char F=0 and char Fv=p, lift any residue-independent tuple over Fp. For a nonzero polynomial over Q, scale by a power of p so that all coefficients are p-integral and some coefficient is a unit. Its reduction cannot vanish at the tuple, so the lifts are Q-algebraically independent. Thus trdeg_Fp(Fv)≤trdeg_Q(F).

The Kronecker dimension of F is trdeg_Q(F)+1 in the second case, while that of Fv is trdeg_Fp(Fv), giving the strict inequality. The argument for all finite independent tuples also shows the residue transcendence degree is finite.

items.name: Positive-characteristic C-field bound
items.statement: If E has characteristic p>0 and finite absolute transcendence degree e, it is C_{e+1}; in particular every quadratic form over E in more than 2^{e+1} variables is isotropic.
items.note: The source uses the usual algebraic-extension-stable C-field theorem; original proof remains a gap.
proofSteps: Finite fields are C_1; adjoining e independent variables raises the C-index by e.
Finite algebraic extensions preserve the bound; arbitrary algebraic extensions reduce every form to finite data.
Apply the degree-two variable-count criterion.

items.name: Finite-stage descent of real-place isotropy
items.statement: In the characteristic-zero residue case of Proposition 3.2(3), choose a residue field of representatives E⊂F and lift the unit coefficients to η∈E. If the original form is isotropic after every real closure of the constant field, there is a finitely generated E'⊂E containing η for which e(q_η) vanishes after every completion/real-closure base change of its constant field. The real-place step uses a projective system of finite bad-place sets and cohomology continuity.
items.note: Includes the coefficient-field and continuity inputs, not established by a name search.
proofSteps: Lift residue coefficients through an equicharacteristic-zero coefficient field in the henselization.
For each nonreal constant place use nonreal-local-cd-bound directly; the printed finite bound on cd(E′) is false for formally real E′ (E6).
Descend coefficients and finitely many cohomology relations to a finitely generated subfield.
Use compactness of the inverse system of real-place bad sets to obtain one finite stage working at every real place.

items.name: Dimension-bound isotropy of unit Pfister forms
items.statement: Let F be a nontrivially henselian non-dyadic valued field of finite Kronecker dimension r, with constant field k. For a unit tuple ε_r,…,ε_0, if q_ε is isotropic over Fk_v for every real closure k_v of k, then q_ε is isotropic over F.
proofSteps: Use the strict residue-dimension drop.
For positive residue characteristic apply the C-field bound.
For characteristic-zero residue use finite descent, the global-base Hasse principle and the Pfister vanishing criterion, then lift residue isotropy.

items.name: Niceness relative to a global subfield
items.statement: For a presented (d+1)-fold Pfister form q_a over an H_d field K and a global subfield k_1⊂K with a_1,a_0∈k_1×, call it k_1-nice if q_{a_1,a_0} is isotropic over k_{1v} whenever v is real, dyadic, has v(a_0)≠0, or has v(a_1)<0. Nice means k_1-nice for some global subfield.
items.note: These two clauses define one predicate and its existential abbreviation; presentation dependence is explicit.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.niceForm.characterise
api.statement: The tail entries a_1,a_0 belong to the specified global subfield.

api.name: DittmannPop.niceForm.structure
api.statement: Each real, dyadic, nonunit-a_0 or negative-a_1 place makes the binary tail isotropic.

api.name: DittmannPop.niceForm.compatibility
api.statement: Changing outer parameters without changing the global tail preserves niceness.

tests.statement: Over Q the tail a_1=a_0=1 is nice and hyperbolic.

tests.name: DittmannPop.niceForm.test2
tests.statement: Over Q the tail a_1=a_0=−1 is not nice because its real form is positive definite.

tests.name: DittmannPop.niceForm.test3

uses.how: Force local anisotropy to occur at a non-dyadic place with odd last coefficient valuation.

items.name: Divisorial detection of a nice anisotropic form
items.statement: For H_d(K), a global subfield k_1⊂K and an anisotropic k_1-nice q_a, some prime divisor w of K has q_a anisotropic over K_w.
proofSteps: Associate a nonzero cohomological Pfister invariant.
Use global-base local–global detection and choose a model at a detecting finite place.
Obtain a regular model through an odd-degree alteration without killing the class; apply model Hasse detection.
In characteristic two use the separate wild Hasse input.

items.name: Parity and residue restrictions at detecting divisors
items.statement: Under Proposition 3.4's hypotheses, if q_a is anisotropic over K_w for a prime divisor w, then w is non-dyadic, w(a_0)=0, w(a_1)>=0, and at least one of w(a_i),1<=i<=d, is odd in the normalized value group Z.
proofSteps: Niceness rules out dyadic, nonunit-a0 and negative-a1 restrictions.
If every remaining parameter value were even, remove squares to leave unit parameters.
Apply dimension-unit-isotropy to contradict the detecting anisotropy.

items.name: Abundance of nice binary tails
items.statement: For a finite separable extension l_1/k_1 of global fields and a finite set Σ of finite places of k_1, there are a_1,a_0∈k_1× whose valuations vanish at every v∈Σ such that q_{a_1,a_0} is k_1-nice and remains anisotropic over l_1.
items.note: Proof uses completely split places, weak and strong approximation, and openness of local norm groups in both global-field characteristics; those inputs need precise suppliers.
proofSteps: Choose a completely split place outside the finite forbidden set and a0 with nonsplit residue binary form there.
Choose another place splitting the quadratic root field and prescribe a1 by strong approximation.
Local norms ensure niceness at all bad places; the odd value at the first split place preserves anisotropy over l1.

items.name: Separating parameters adapted to a geometric divisor
items.statement: For H_d(K) and a geometric prime divisor w, there is a global subfield k_1 and an algebraically independent tuple u_{d−1},…,u_2 such that w is trivial on k_1(u) and Kw/k_1(u) is finite separable. Every u_d∈K with w(u_d)=1 extends u to a separating transcendence basis of K/k_1.
items.note: The inseparable-part argument uses the defectless fundamental equality for one-variable function fields; not general defectlessness of all valued fields.
proofSteps: Lift a separating residue transcendence basis and choose the constant/global subfield separately in each characteristic.
Add a uniformizer to obtain a transcendence basis upstairs.
For the remaining purely inseparable subextension, e=f=1; use the one-variable function-field fundamental equality to force degree one.

items.name: Test form for a distinguished element
items.statement: For H_d(K), global k_1⊂K, algebraically independent t_{d−1},…,t_2 over k_1 and a_d∈K×, a k_1,t-test form is a k_1-nice q_{a_d,…,a_0} with a_i=t_i−ε_i for 2<=i<d, where ε_i∈k_1× are units at every finite place v with v(a_1)>0.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.statement: Extract the k_1-niceness predicate.

api.name: DittmannPop.testForm.structure
api.statement: Extract a_i=t_i−ε_i and ε_i∈k_1× for 2<=i<d.

api.name: DittmannPop.testForm.compatibility
api.statement: Each ε_i is a unit at every finite place where a_1 has positive value.

tests.statement: Every test form has a nice tail.

tests.name: DittmannPop.testForm.test2
tests.statement: With transcendental t over Q and tail a_1=a_0=1, ε_2=1 satisfies the unit condition.

tests.name: DittmannPop.testForm.test3

items.name: Abundant test forms at a prescribed divisor
items.statement: For H_d(K), geometric w, and global k_1 plus algebraically independent t such that w is trivial on k_1(t) and Kw/k_1(t) is finite separable, there is a Zariski open dense U⊂(k_1×)^{d−2} such that for each ε∈U a k_1-nice tail can be chosen so that every a_d with w(a_d) odd yields an anisotropic k_1,t-test form over K_w.
items.note: One tail per epsilon works for all odd-valuation a_d; requires finite normalization, its étale locus and the local power-series embedding. The paper correctly chooses Σ so every ε_i is a Σ-unit: this means a unit outside Σ. Thus Σ contains every nonunit place, and Lemma 3.5 makes a_1 a unit at each of them. This is a clarification, not a source error.
proofSteps: Choose ε in the étale locus of the normalized torus and embed its function field into iterated Laurent series.
Apply global-nice-tail to the finite separable residue extension, taking the forbidden places to contain the nonunit places of ε.
Independent-value isotropy for the Laurent parameters and the odd value of a_d imply anisotropy.

items.name: Patch topology of the valuation spectrum
items.statement: The valuation spectrum Spv(A) of a commutative ring A has the topology induced by its injective relation-table map v↦((f,s)↦[v(f)<=v(s)]) into the Boolean product indexed by A×A.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.patchSpectrum.characterise
api.statement: Extract the Boolean valuation-comparison table.

api.name: DittmannPop.patchSpectrum.structure
api.statement: Equal comparison tables give equal spectrum points.

api.name: DittmannPop.patchSpectrum.compatibility
api.statement: Basic valuation comparisons with nonzero denominator are patch-clopen.

tests.name: DittmannPop.patchSpectrum.test1
tests.statement: The trivial valuation is a point of Spv(F).

tests.name: DittmannPop.patchSpectrum.test2
tests.statement: In the library's MULTIPLICATIVE convention, every point satisfies v(0)<=v(1) and not v(1)<=v(0).

tests.name: DittmannPop.patchSpectrum.test3
tests.statement: For a field, valuation-ring membership a∈O_v is patch-clopen after the additive/multiplicative convention conversion.

uses.how: Make the finitely many polynomial valuation conditions clopen.

items.name: Compactness of the patch valuation spectrum
items.statement: For every commutative ring A the relation-table map of Spv(A) with its patch topology is a closed embedding into (A×A→Bool), and this patch space is compact. It is Hausdorff by the embedding into the Boolean product.
proofSteps: Use the pinned closed embedding into the Boolean product.
Compactness follows from the existing instance; the field-specific membership dictionary is a separate item.

items.name: Valuation rings and the field patch topology
items.statement: For a field F, identify equivalence classes of valuations with valuation subrings and with Spv(F). The induced topology is the coarsest making {v:a∈O_v} clopen for every a∈F. For b≠0, a pairwise valuation comparison reduces to membership of a/b, so no new compactness proof is needed.
items.note: Adapter is missing even though the compactness input is built.
proofSteps: Over a field every valuation has zero support and yields a valuation subring.
For nonzero denominator convert comparisons into membership of ratios, translating additive/multiplicative conventions.
The two Boolean topologies therefore coincide, importing compactness.

items.name: Open locus of henselian embeddings
items.statement: For a finite extension E/F the set of valuations w on F such that E admits an F-embedding into F_w is patch-open. If nonempty, E/F is separable; at each such w a henselian generator and derivative-unit condition give a clopen neighborhood.
items.note: Uses Kuhlmann–Novacoski Theorem 1.2 for the generator; original proof not read.
proofSteps: Choose the henselian generator and an approximate root x in F.
The finite coefficient-integrality, positive-polynomial-value and unit-derivative conditions define a patch-clopen neighborhood.
At every valuation in that neighborhood Hensel's lemma gives the required root and embedding.

items.name: Open locus of henselian isotropy
items.statement: For a quadratic form q over F the valuations w such that q is isotropic over F_w form a patch-open subset: an isotropic vector is defined over a finite subextension E/F of F_w and the embedding-open locus of E supplies a neighborhood.
proofSteps: An isotropic vector over a henselization has finitely many algebraic coordinates.
Descend it to a finite intermediate extension and use its patch-open embedding locus.

items.name: Quadratic changes of transcendence parameters
items.statement: For u_{d−1},…,u_2 algebraically independent over global k_1, put t_i=u_i²−u_i. Then k_1(u)/k_1(t) is finite separable, generated by these quadratic equations, and their relative algebraic closures in K agree. This construction is used in every characteristic.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.quadraticParameters.characterise
api.statement: For every i, u_i²−u_i=t_i.

api.name: DittmannPop.quadraticParameters.structure
api.statement: The involution u_i↦1−u_i preserves t_i.

api.name: DittmannPop.quadraticParameters.compatibility
api.statement: The relative closures of k_1(u) and k_1(t) in K agree.

tests.name: DittmannPop.quadraticParameters.test1
tests.statement: u and 1−u give the same quadratic parameter.

tests.name: DittmannPop.quadraticParameters.test2
tests.statement: In characteristic two the involution is u↦u+1.

tests.name: DittmannPop.quadraticParameters.test3
tests.statement: For transcendental u the extension k(u)/k(u²−u) is separable of degree two.

uses.how: Translate the coordinate substitutions into test inequalities for the compactness argument.

items.name: Auxiliary quadratic root fields
items.statement: Fix a_d∈K×. For θ∈K× and τ∈K choose roots α²−α=a_d/θ² and β²−β=τ²/a_d in an algebraic closure, and set K_θ=K(α), K_τ=K(β), K_{θ,τ}=K(α,β). These are finite separable extensions (possibly trivial); different root choices give K-isomorphic fields.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.auxiliaryQuadraticField.characterise
api.statement: Extract both generator equations.

api.name: DittmannPop.auxiliaryQuadraticField.structure
api.statement: The two root fields generate the compositum K_{θ,τ}.

api.name: DittmannPop.auxiliaryQuadraticField.compatibility
api.statement: Conjugating either generator by z↦1−z leaves its root field unchanged.

tests.name: DittmannPop.auxiliaryQuadraticField.test1
tests.statement: τ=0 gives K_τ=K.

tests.name: DittmannPop.auxiliaryQuadraticField.test2
tests.statement: A generator already in K gives a trivial field extension.

tests.name: DittmannPop.auxiliaryQuadraticField.test3
tests.statement: In characteristic two the derivative of X²−X−c is −1.

uses.how: Test isotropy over actual root fields, including trivial adjunctions.

items.name: Nonnegative coefficients in the auxiliary detection argument
items.statement: In Proposition 3.10 fix N>0, θ=(a_{d−1}⋯a_1)^N and a detecting divisor w̃ of L(α). Then w̃(a_i)>=0 for i<d. Negative value of t_i−ε_i would make it a square times a principal unit and force isotropy.
items.note: Use a'_i=1−1/u_i−ε_i/u_i²; the printed plus sign on epsilon is a harmless-to-principal-unit but not literal algebraic identity.
proofSteps: If a_i=t_i−ε_i had negative value, the u_i²−u_i presentation makes u_i have negative value.
Divide by u_i²: the remaining factor is 1−1/u_i−ε_i/u_i², a principal unit.
Principal-unit isotropy contradicts detection; the minus sign before ε_i is essential in the identity.

items.name: Arbitrarily strong coefficient domination
items.statement: With the same data, w̃(a_d)>N w̃(a_i) for every i<d and w̃(a_d)>0. If w̃(a_d)<2w̃(θ), the root equation again makes a_d a square times a principal unit.
proofSteps: Compare a_d with θ² using the auxiliary quadratic equation.
In the prohibited value range divide by a square and obtain a principal-unit factor.
Eliminate the zero-value case by dimension-unit-isotropy to obtain strict positivity.

items.name: Compactness produces an infinitely dominating valuation
items.statement: If the anisotropy hypotheses of Proposition 3.10 hold for every N>0, the nested patch-closed nonempty sets of valuations w on L for which q_a is anisotropic over L_w, w(a_i)>=0 and w(a_d)>Nw(a_i) have a common point w_a.
proofSteps: Each finite N has a detecting valuation by the previous claims.
Anisotropy is patch-closed, and finite value inequalities are clopen.
The closed sets are nested; compactness yields one valuation meeting every N-bound.

items.name: Coarsening at an infinitely large coefficient
items.statement: For a valued field (F,w) and a∈F with γ=w(a)>0, put p={x∈F: γ<=Nw(x) for some positive integer N}, with zero included. This is a prime ideal of O_w. Localization (O_w)_p is a valuation ring coarsening w. If b≠0, w(b)>=0 and Nw(b)<γ for every N>0, b becomes a unit; a stays in the maximal ideal.
proofSteps: For nonzero x, membership implies w(x)>0. Closure under multiplication by O_w and addition follows from monotonicity and the valuation inequality, using the larger of two witnessing integers.
If x,y are nonmembers, then Nw(x)<gamma and Nw(y)<gamma for every positive N. Applying this at 2N shows N(w(x)+w(y))<gamma, so xy is a nonmember; hence p is prime.

Consume Mathlib ValuationSubring.ofPrime and its localization instance, ofPrime_valuation_eq_one_iff_mem_primeCompl, and idealOfLE_ofPrime. The DP-specific work is the explicit prime and its coefficient inequalities, not a new localization/coarsening carrier.

api.name: DittmannPop.coarseningPrime.characterise
api.statement: Membership is γ<=Nw(x) for some N>0, including zero.

api.name: DittmannPop.coarseningPrime.structure
api.statement: Localization at this prime ideal gives the coarsened valuation ring.

api.name: DittmannPop.coarseningPrime.compatibility
api.statement: If 0<=w(b) and Nw(b)<γ for all N>0, b becomes a unit.

tests.name: DittmannPop.coarseningPrime.test1
tests.statement: For a discrete valuation and γ=1, this prime is the maximal ideal.

tests.name: DittmannPop.coarseningPrime.test2
tests.statement: For lexicographic Z² and γ=(1,0), value (0,1) becomes a unit.

tests.name: DittmannPop.coarseningPrime.test3
tests.statement: In that Z² example a positive first coordinate puts an element in the prime even if the second coordinate is negative.

uses.how: Localize the valuation ring at the prime obtained from domination by the last coefficient.

items.name: Henselizations under valuation coarsening
items.statement: For a coarsening w_L of w_a, compatible embeddings identify L_{w_L} with a subfield of L_{w_a}; consequently anisotropy over the latter implies anisotropy over the former.
proofSteps: Compare decomposition groups or use the universal property of compatible henselizations under a valuation coarsening.
Embed the coarser henselization in the finer one; an isotropic vector upstairs in the former would contradict anisotropy in the latter.

items.name: Triviality on the lower-dimensional base
items.statement: The coarsened w_L in Proposition 3.10 is trivial on k_1(t). Nontriviality on k_1, then on k_1(t), each contradicts dimension-unit-isotropy for the unit tail. Since L/k_1(t) has transcendence degree one, w_L is a prime divisor.
items.note: The source's 'q_a is isotropic over F_v' should read q_ε: a_d need not lie in F (E15).
proofSteps: Localize at the explicitly defined prime so lower parameters become units but a_d remains positive.
A nontrivial restriction to constants or k1(t) would force isotropy of the unit tail.
Use the one-variable discreteness theorem and residue-dimension comparison to identify a relative prime divisor.

items.name: Refined positive odd divisor detection
items.statement: Let H_d(K), L/K finite separable, a_d∈K×, k_1 global and u algebraically independent, t=u²−u. If a k_1,t-test form q_a stays anisotropic over L(α), α²−α=a_d/(a_{d−1}⋯a_1)^{2N}, for every N>0, then a prime divisor w_L of L trivial on k_1(t) satisfies w_L(a_d)>0 odd and q_a is anisotropic over L_{w_L}.
proofSteps: Combine the compact detecting valuation with its coarsening.
Apply the parity result once the coarsened prime divisor has been identified.

items.name: The relative constant field k_t
items.statement: For k_1 and t=u²−u as above, k_t is the relative algebraic closure of k_1(t) in K; it equals k_u. Then K/k_t is a one-variable function field with k_t relatively algebraically closed in K.
items.note: Use the existing algebraicClosure carrier over IntermediateField.adjoin k_1 t. The equality k_t=k_u and the one-variable-function-field consequence are the new DP adapters.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.relativeConstantField.characterise
api.statement: Membership means algebraicity over k_1(t).

api.name: DittmannPop.relativeConstantField.structure
api.statement: Algebraicity of k_1(u)/k_1(t) gives k_u=k_t.

api.name: DittmannPop.relativeConstantField.compatibility
api.statement: K/k_t is a one-variable function field with k_t relatively algebraically closed.

tests.name: DittmannPop.relativeConstantField.test1
tests.statement: In k_1(u,v), the relative closure of k_1(u²−u) is k_1(u).

tests.name: DittmannPop.relativeConstantField.test2
tests.statement: Every u_i belongs to k_t.

tests.name: DittmannPop.relativeConstantField.test3
tests.statement: In k_1(u,v), v does not belong to this k_t.

uses.how: Require the detecting valuation to be trivial on the algebraic constants of the selected rational subfield.

items.name: Universal auxiliary anisotropy set
items.statement: For the fixed test data a, define b_a={τ∈K: q_a is anisotropic over K_{θ,τ} for every θ∈k_t×}. The universal quantifier ranges over the definable relative subfield, not all of K×.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.anisotropySet.characterise
api.statement: Membership universally quantifies θ over k_t×.

api.name: DittmannPop.anisotropySet.structure
api.statement: Changing the auxiliary root choices leaves membership unchanged.

api.name: DittmannPop.anisotropySet.compatibility
api.statement: For admissible test data b_a equals the union of the detecting balls.

tests.name: DittmannPop.anisotropySet.test1
tests.statement: V_a empty implies b_a empty, hence zero is not a member.

tests.name: DittmannPop.anisotropySet.test2
tests.statement: For singleton V_a, b_a equals that one ball.

tests.name: DittmannPop.anisotropySet.test3
tests.statement: For nonempty V_a, zero belongs to b_a.

uses.how: Identify the root-field anisotropy locus with a union of valuation balls.

items.name: Multiplicative stabilizer of the anisotropy set
items.statement: Set O_a={x∈K: for every τ∈b_a, xτ∈b_a}. No assertion that this is a valuation ring is built into its definition.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.stabilizerRing.characterise
api.statement: x belongs iff it sends every element of b_a into b_a by multiplication.

api.name: DittmannPop.stabilizerRing.structure
api.statement: For admissible data it is the intersection of the detecting valuation rings.

api.name: DittmannPop.stabilizerRing.compatibility
api.statement: The stabilizer of the empty set is K.

tests.name: DittmannPop.stabilizerRing.test1
tests.statement: Stab(empty)=K.

tests.name: DittmannPop.stabilizerRing.test2
tests.statement: The stabilizer of a discrete valuation's maximal ideal is its valuation ring.

tests.name: DittmannPop.stabilizerRing.test3
tests.statement: The scalar 1 belongs even when b_a is empty.

uses.how: Recover the intersection of valuation rings from multiplicative preservation of the union.

items.name: Finite set of detecting divisors
items.statement: V_a consists of prime divisors w of K trivial on k_t for which w(a_d)>0 and q_a is anisotropic over K_w. It is finite because positive valuations of a fixed rational function on its normal proper curve have finite support.
items.note: The source writes D_{K|k_a} for D_{K|k_t} twice on p. 14 (E16).
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.detectingDivisorSet.characterise
api.statement: Membership requires triviality on k_t, positive value of a_d and henselian anisotropy.

api.name: DittmannPop.detectingDivisorSet.structure
api.statement: The set is finite, being inside the zero-support of a_d.

api.name: DittmannPop.detectingDivisorSet.compatibility
api.statement: Every member has positive odd normalized value on a_d.

tests.name: DittmannPop.detectingDivisorSet.test1
tests.statement: If q_a is isotropic over K then V_a is empty.

tests.name: DittmannPop.detectingDivisorSet.test2
tests.statement: If a_d has no relative zero then V_a is empty.

tests.name: DittmannPop.detectingDivisorSet.test3
tests.statement: The isolation construction gives exactly {w}.

uses.how: Use finite support and a prescribed odd pole to isolate one desired divisor.

items.name: Odd-threshold valuation ball
items.statement: For w∈V_a put b_w={τ∈K: 2w(τ)>w(a_d)}. With w normalized and w(a_d)=2m+1>0 this is {τ:w(τ)>=m+1}, including zero.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.valuationBall.characterise
api.statement: τ belongs iff 2w(τ)>w(a_d), with w(0)=infinity.

api.name: DittmannPop.valuationBall.structure
api.statement: For w(a_d)=2m+1 its threshold is w(τ)>=m+1.

api.name: DittmannPop.valuationBall.compatibility
api.statement: Addition and multiplication by O_w preserve the ball.

tests.name: DittmannPop.valuationBall.test1
tests.statement: For w(a_d)=1 the ball is the maximal ideal.

tests.name: DittmannPop.valuationBall.test2
tests.statement: For w(a_d)=3 value 1 is excluded and value 2 is included.

tests.name: DittmannPop.valuationBall.test3
tests.statement: Zero belongs to the ball.

uses.how: Use the strict inequality 2w(τ)>w(a_d), including parity and τ=0 conventions.

items.name: A valuation ball recovers its ring
items.statement: For a nontrivial discrete valuation w and any integer threshold c, the multiplicative stabilizer of {τ:w(τ)>=c} equals O_w. In particular it recovers O_w from b_w above.
proofSteps: Nonnegative-value scalars preserve the threshold.
For a negative-value scalar choose an element of exact threshold using a uniformizer; its product falls outside.

items.name: Auxiliary anisotropy is a union of balls
items.statement: For data of Notations 4.1 in an H_d field, b_a=⋃_{w∈V_a}b_w. The reverse inclusion uses Hensel roots of both auxiliary equations; the forward inclusion applies refined-detection to L=K_τ and uses odd parity to obtain a strict inequality.
proofSteps: If τ lies in a detecting ball, both auxiliary roots lie in the corresponding henselization, preserving anisotropy.
Conversely apply refined-detection to K_τ; restrict the resulting divisor to K.
The root equation and odd parity give 2w(τ)>w(a_d).

items.name: Stabilizer equals an intersection of valuation rings
items.statement: For the same data, O_a=⋂_{w∈V_a}O_w. If x has negative valuation at one w, weak approximation constructs y∈b_w with minimal w-value but xy outside every b_{w'}; this proves the nontrivial inclusion. Empty V_a gives b_a=empty and O_a=K.
items.note: Requires independent finite valuations and weak approximation, not the false claim that stabilization of any union equals the intersection of all stabilizers.
proofSteps: Every scalar integral at all detecting divisors preserves the union of balls.
If x has negative value at one divisor, weak approximation chooses y at that ball's minimal threshold and arranges xy outside every other ball.
Handle the empty set separately: its stabilizer is the whole field.

items.name: One prescribed pole in a function field
items.statement: For fields k⊂F with F a one-variable function field and k relatively algebraically closed in F, every place P and natural n>=2g admit f≠0 with ord_P(f)=−n and ord_Q(f)>=0 for every Q≠P. For n>0 this gives pole divisor nP.
proofSteps: Apply the pinned high-degree prescribed-pole theorem with n>=2g.
The downstream use chooses n positive and odd; no scheme-side Riemann–Roch is rebuilt.

items.name: Isolation of one geometric prime divisor
items.statement: For every geometric prime divisor w of H_d(K), choose k_1,u and test data with V_a={w}. Choose an odd m>=2g and a function with sole pole mP, take a_d=1/f, and use test-abundance. Then O_w is the multiplicative stabilizer of b_a.
proofSteps: Choose separating data and its quadratic transform.
Use a function with sole pole of positive odd order, taking a_d to be its inverse.
Choose the test tail by test-abundance; finite zero support now isolates precisely w.

items.name: First-order valuation-ring filter
items.statement: Express admissibility of all test parameters and the definition of O_a in the ring language. Retain a fiber only if O_a is a proper valuation subring (for every x≠0, x or x^{-1} belongs); otherwise define the empty fiber. A finite intersection of the pairwise independent divisor rings is a proper valuation ring only when it is a single one.
items.note: Includes a finite-intersection lemma and parameter guard; neither is hidden in an informal instruction to check valuation.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.valuationFilter.characterise
api.statement: A nonempty accepted fiber has admissible parameters and is a proper valuation ring.

api.name: DittmannPop.valuationFilter.structure
api.statement: Rejected parameter tuples give the empty fiber.

api.name: DittmannPop.valuationFilter.compatibility
api.statement: Every isolated geometric divisor is attained.

tests.name: DittmannPop.valuationFilter.test1
tests.statement: A candidate equal to K is rejected.

tests.name: DittmannPop.valuationFilter.test2
tests.statement: A candidate missing both x and x^{-1} for some x≠0 is rejected.

tests.name: DittmannPop.valuationFilter.test3
tests.statement: An isolated divisor's parameters return exactly its valuation ring.

uses.how: Reject the whole field and all non-proper valuation-ring candidates so invalid parameters give empty fibers.

items.name: Uniform divisors in Kronecker dimensions one and two
items.statement: In dimension one, prime divisors of global fields are uniformly definable; geometric ones occur precisely for global function fields. In dimension two, geometric prime divisors are uniformly definable by Pop's curve-over-global-field theorem after choosing a global subfield on which the divisor is trivial.
items.locator: Remark 4.4, Rumely Introduction I–II and Pop 2017 Theorem 1.2
items.note: Original Rumely and Pop proofs not yet read; must keep arithmetic places of number fields out of the geometric family.
proofSteps: Use Rumely's global-field family at dimension one.
Use Pop's function-field-of-a-curve-over-global-field result at dimension two.
Keep these as source-qualified inputs until the original definitions and proofs are audited.

items.name: First-order detection of Kronecker dimension
items.statement: For every nonnegative integer d there is a ring sentence which, among finitely generated fields, holds exactly in those of Kronecker dimension d.
proofSteps: Import the fixed-dimension sentence from the results summarized in Poonen Theorem 2.3.
Separate characteristic-zero and positive-characteristic Kronecker shifts.

items.name: Uniform definition of constants
items.statement: There is a ring formula ψ(t), independent of the finitely generated field K, whose solutions are exactly the relative algebraic closure κ of the prime field in K.
proofSteps: Use Poonen Theorem 1.3, whose proof is in the selected §5 reading.
Record its internal elliptic/global-subfield ingredients as remaining source leaves.

items.name: Uniform family of maximal global subfields
items.statement: The relatively algebraically closed global subfields k_1 of a finitely generated field K form a uniformly definable family. In characteristic zero the unique such field is κ; in positive characteristic use Poonen Proposition 4.10. A dimension-one filter excludes other subfields.
items.locator: §4 opening and Notations 4.1(1); Poonen Lemma 3.7, Proposition 4.10
items.note: Poonen Theorem 1.4 by itself states absolute dependence, not this family; the extraction supplies the actual locators.
proofSteps: In characteristic zero use the definable constant field.
In positive characteristic use Poonen Proposition 4.10's family.
Apply the dimension-one and relative-algebraic-closure conditions to select the intended global subfields.

items.name: Definable algebraic independence over a global subfield
items.statement: For each n, a formula in the ring language augmented with a predicate for a relatively algebraically closed global subfield L detects whether an n-tuple in a finitely generated extension K/L is algebraically dependent over L; negate it for independence.
proofSteps: Use Poonen Lemma 5.3 with an explicit predicate for the global subfield.
Replace that predicate by its uniform defining formula and negate dependence.

items.name: First-order translation through quadratic extensions
items.statement: For fixed Pfister length and parameters defining K_θ,K_τ, express isotropy and anisotropy after their compositum by finitely many ring formulas on basis coordinates, splitting the cases of a root already in the field, a genuine quadratic extension, and collapse of the second extension. The translation is equivalent to anisotropy over the root FIELD, not over a reducible quotient algebra.
items.note: Necessary explicit bridge; the paper treats bounded finite-extension interpretation as standard.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.quadraticExtensionFormulas.characterise
api.statement: Translate equality and operations using a basis of each genuine quadratic extension.

api.name: DittmannPop.quadraticExtensionFormulas.structure
api.statement: Split off the cases in which a root already lies in the base or the second adjunction collapses.

api.name: DittmannPop.quadraticExtensionFormulas.compatibility
api.statement: Isotropy over the root field agrees with the translated existential formula and anisotropy with its negation.

tests.name: DittmannPop.quadraticExtensionFormulas.test1
tests.statement: If τ=0 the second extension translation reduces to the first extension only.

tests.name: DittmannPop.quadraticExtensionFormulas.test2
tests.statement: For X²−X with both roots in K, the translation uses K, not the split algebra K×K.

tests.name: DittmannPop.quadraticExtensionFormulas.test3
tests.statement: In characteristic≠2 when 1+4c=0, adjoining a root of X²−X−c gives K, not a quadratic field.

uses.how: Encode isotropy in quadratic root fields by ring formulas with explicit split/trivial branches.

items.name: Integral closure generated by a transcendence basis
items.statement: For a transcendence basis T of finitely generated K over its prime field, let R_T be the integral closure in K of the subring generated by T. Writing κ for constants and A=κ in characteristic p or O_κ in characteristic zero, the same ring is the integral closure of A[T] in K.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.normalizationRing.characterise
api.statement: Membership is integrality over the prime-ring algebra generated by T.

api.name: DittmannPop.normalizationRing.structure
api.statement: This equals the integral closure of A[T] with A=κ or O_κ.

api.name: DittmannPop.normalizationRing.compatibility
api.statement: Its fraction field is K.

tests.name: DittmannPop.normalizationRing.test1
tests.statement: For Q(t), R_{t}=Z[t].

tests.name: DittmannPop.normalizationRing.test2
tests.statement: For F_q(t), R_{t}=F_q[t].

uses.how: Obtain a finite module over A[T] and a finitely generated domain with fraction field K.

items.name: Finiteness of the normalization ring
items.statement: R_T is finite as an A[T]-module and is consequently a finitely generated integral domain over the prime ring; its fraction field is K. The required finiteness is for arbitrary finite extensions in positive characteristic, including inseparable ones.
items.locator: Proposition 5.1 proof; Eisenbud Corollary 13.13 and Proposition 13.14
items.note: Separability-only integral-closure theorems do not cover the full statement.
proofSteps: Apply finite-normalization-generic to A[T]⊂K.
Finite module generation over the finitely generated prime-ring algebra implies finite ring generation.
Localization of the integral closure has fraction field K.

items.name: Normalization over the constant field
items.statement: S_T is the integral closure of κ[T] in K. Let W_T be the geometric prime divisors w of K with T⊂O_w. This W_T is a rank-one family, distinct from the maximal-rank flags used later in characteristic zero.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.geometricNormalization.characterise
api.statement: Membership in S_T is integrality over κ[T].

api.name: DittmannPop.geometricNormalization.structure
api.statement: W_T comprises rank-one geometric prime divisors integral on T.

api.name: DittmannPop.geometricNormalization.compatibility
api.statement: S_T is the intersection of their valuation rings.

tests.name: DittmannPop.geometricNormalization.test1
tests.statement: For Q(t), S_{t}=Q[t] while R_{t}=Z[t].

tests.name: DittmannPop.geometricNormalization.test2
tests.statement: For F_q(t), S_{t}=R_{t}.

tests.name: DittmannPop.geometricNormalization.test3
tests.statement: The pole-at-infinity place of t is not in W_T.

uses.how: Intersect rank-one geometric divisors integral on the chosen basis.

items.name: Geometric normalization as a divisorial intersection
items.statement: S_T=⋂_{w∈W_T}O_w. One inclusion uses integrality of valuation rings; the other uses the intersection of height-one localizations of the normal noetherian domain S_T. Consequently S_T is definable using the uniform divisor formula.
items.note: The underlying Krull-domain intersection input needs its own library check.
proofSteps: Every valuation ring containing T and κ contains S_T by integrality.
Conversely height-one localizations of normal S_T are geometric prime-divisor rings containing T.
Intersect using the Krull-domain theorem, then translate the universal quantifier over the definable family.

items.name: Full-rank geometric valuation flags
items.statement: In characteristic zero let e=trdeg(K/κ). A geometric prime e-divisor is a valuation trivial on κ with ordered value group Z^e in lexicographic order, obtained by composing e geometric rank-one residue valuations. Its final residue field κ_w is a finite extension of κ. Denote by G_T those for which T⊂O_w.
items.note: Uses a new symbol G_T to resolve the printed reuse of rank-one W_T in the subsequent V_T formula.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.maximalGeometricFlags.characterise
api.statement: A full e-step geometric flag has value group Z^e lexicographically.

api.name: DittmannPop.maximalGeometricFlags.structure
api.statement: Its final residue field is finite over κ.

api.name: DittmannPop.maximalGeometricFlags.compatibility
api.statement: G_T requires the full composite valuation to be nonnegative on T.

tests.name: DittmannPop.maximalGeometricFlags.test1
tests.statement: For Q(t), e=1 and the final residue is a number field.

tests.name: DittmannPop.maximalGeometricFlags.test2
tests.statement: In Q(t_1,t_2), the single divisor t_1=0 is not a full rank-two flag.

tests.name: DittmannPop.maximalGeometricFlags.test3
tests.statement: The flag t_1=0 followed by t_2=0 has final residue Q.

uses.how: Iterate geometric residues until the final residue is a number field before using arithmetic primes.

items.name: Definable residue field
items.statement: If O_w⊂F is a definable valuation ring, its maximal ideal is definable from nonunits, and the quotient O_w/m_w with its residue map is interpretable as a definable quotient in F.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.residueInterpretation.characterise
api.statement: The maximal ideal consists of zero and nonunits of O_w.

api.name: DittmannPop.residueInterpretation.structure
api.statement: Representatives have equal residues iff their difference is in that ideal.

api.name: DittmannPop.residueInterpretation.compatibility
api.statement: Addition and multiplication descend from O_w.

tests.name: DittmannPop.residueInterpretation.test1
tests.statement: The p-adic valuation ring of Q has interpreted residue F_p.

tests.name: DittmannPop.residueInterpretation.test2
tests.statement: Representatives differing by an element of the maximal ideal agree.

tests.name: DittmannPop.residueInterpretation.test3
tests.statement: Every unit has nonzero residue.

uses.how: Compose the definable quotient interpretations along a fixed-length valuation flag.

items.name: Definability of composite valuations
items.statement: If O_{w'}⊂F and O_{w''}⊂Fw' are definable, the composite valuation ring is the inverse image of O_{w''} under O_{w'}→Fw'. It is definable in F after translating through the residue interpretation; an iterated fixed-length family remains uniform.
proofSteps: Define nonunits of O_w as the maximal ideal and interpret the residue field by its equality kernel.
Pull the second valuation predicate back to representatives.
Iterate a fixed number of times, retaining all parameters.

items.name: Arithmetic refinements of geometric flags
items.statement: In characteristic zero set V_T={v∘w: w∈G_T, v a finite prime of the number field κ_w=Kw, and each t∈T lies in O_{v∘w}}. Its members are full-rank arithmetic valuation rings, not merely discrete rank-one rings.
items.note: The full-rank interpretation is required by finiteness of κ_w; the printed W_T notation is ambiguous.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.arithmeticFlags.characterise
api.statement: Extract a full-rank geometric prefix with finite number-field residue.

api.name: DittmannPop.arithmeticFlags.structure
api.statement: The final factor is a finite prime of that residue number field.

api.name: DittmannPop.arithmeticFlags.compatibility
api.statement: Every parameter of T has nonnegative composite value.

tests.name: DittmannPop.arithmeticFlags.test1
tests.statement: For Q(t), t=0 followed by the p-adic place gives a permitted flag.

tests.name: DittmannPop.arithmeticFlags.test2
tests.statement: A lone geometric divisor on Q(t_1,t_2) cannot provide a number-field residue for the final step.

tests.name: DittmannPop.arithmeticFlags.test3
tests.statement: A real place is not an allowed final factor.

uses.how: Append a finite number-field prime to a full geometric flag to detect a nonintegral polynomial coefficient.

items.name: Arithmetic normalization from composed valuations
items.statement: In characteristic zero, R_T=⋂_{v∘w∈V_T}O_{v∘w}. Reduce finite extensions to K_0=κ(T) using prolongation of valuation rings and integral-closure detection, then detect every nonintegral coefficient of a polynomial with a residue-specialization flag.
proofSteps: One inclusion follows from integrality in every arithmetic flag ring.
Use all finite-extension prolongations to reduce to K=κ(T).
Full geometric flags remove non-polynomial elements; coefficient detection then removes nonintegral coefficients.

items.name: Flags detect a nonintegral polynomial coefficient
items.statement: For K_0=κ(T), a finite place v of κ and f=cg with g∈O_v[T] having nonzero reduction, choose a tuple ζ in (κv^alg×)^e where gbar(ζ)≠0, lift all its coordinates to prime-to-residue-characteristic roots of unity, and use the associated full-rank geometric flag plus a prolongation v'. Then g is a unit for v'∘w and nonintegrality of c forces nonintegrality of f.
items.note: Choose ζ in the torus, possible since a nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on every torus point over an infinite algebraic closure; this makes the roots-of-unity lifting literal.
proofSteps: Choose a nonzero residue evaluation on the algebraic torus, so every coordinate is nonzero.
Lift coordinates to roots of unity of order prime to the residue characteristic.
The full-rank flag plus prolonged finite place makes g a unit and records the valuation of c.

items.name: Definability of the finitely generated normalization ring
items.statement: For H_d(K) and transcendence basis T, R_T is a parameter-definable finitely generated domain with fraction field K. In characteristic p it is S_T; in characteristic zero use V_T and arithmetic-intersection.
proofSteps: Use definable constants and the rank-one geometric normalization intersection.
In characteristic zero iterate residue interpretations to obtain full-rank geometric flags, then use uniform global-prime predicates.
Apply arithmetic-intersection; finite generation was proved separately.

items.name: Uniformity for fixed dimension
items.statement: For each fixed d the formula defining R_T can be chosen uniformly for H_d fields, with the elements of T among its parameter variables. This does not assert a parameter-free definition of each normalization.
proofSteps: For fixed d every tuple length and flag length is fixed.
Replace individual parameters and basis elements by formula variables; quantify over each definable family.

items.name: Interpretation of a fraction field
items.statement: For an integral domain R, represent Frac(R) by pairs (a,b)∈R×(R\{0}), modulo (a,b)~(c,d) iff ad=bc; field operations and equality have definable graphs. The quotient is an interpretation, not necessarily a definable subset of R itself.
proofSteps: Use the explicit formula or construction in the statement; the API below specifies its projections, semantic comparisons and downstream laws. Those laws are planning contracts, not implementation claims.

api.name: DittmannPop.fractionInterpretation.characterise
api.statement: Cross multiplication characterizes equality of valid pairs.

tests.name: DittmannPop.fractionInterpretation.test3
tests.statement: Pairs with denominator zero are excluded.

uses.how: Recover the field from its definable normalization domain with a definable identification of fraction pairs.

items.name: Bi-interpretation with the definable normalization
items.statement: If R⊂K is the definable normalization domain above and Frac(R)=K, the residue-free fraction-pair interpretation and the definable inclusion of R in K form a bi-interpretation. The composite identifications are x↦[(a,b)] with bx=a and r↦[(r,1)].
proofSteps: Interpret K as fraction pairs in R_T.
The equation bx=a identifies a field element with its fraction class.
The pair (r,1) identifies the composite copy of R_T, with the fixed definition parameters represented by fraction pairs.

items.name: Integer arithmetic in an infinite finitely generated domain
items.statement: Every infinite finitely generated integral domain, in the ring language, is parametrically bi-interpretable with Z. This theorem is about finite ring generation and is applied to R_T, not directly to K as a ring.
items.note: AKNS §3.2 proof read; its normalization and interpretation lemmas remain explicit source-audit leaves.
proofSteps: Use AKNS Theorem 3.1; its §3.2 proof reduces through Noether normalization and finite extensions to one-dimensional arithmetic.
The graph comparison for polynomial rings is controlled by evaluation and the selected coding lemmas.
Unaudited §3.1/coding and global-number-field leaves remain explicit.

items.name: Bi-interpretability yields quasi-finite axiomatizability
items.statement: Let L be a finite language and A a finitely generated L-structure bi-interpretable with Z. For a finite generating tuple a there is a formula φ_A(x) such that, for every finitely generated L-structure B and tuple b, B⊨φ_A(b) iff an L-isomorphism A→B sends a to b. Existentially quantifying x gives the corresponding sentence within this class.
items.note: Keep the finite-generation-of-L-structure premise. AKNS Lemma 2.29 imports a coding/standardness argument whose external proof is not yet audited.
proofSteps: Use AKNS Proposition 2.28 for a finitely generated structure in a finite language.
Its coding and rigidity lemmas produce a formula fixing the image of a generating tuple.
Existentially quantify that tuple to obtain one sentence; constants are not left in the concluding language.

items.name: From field generation to the ring-language sentence
items.statement: Expand the ring language by total inversion with graph (x=0∧y=0)∨xy=1. A finitely generated field is finitely generated in this finite expanded language; definitional expansion preserves parametric bi-interpretability. Apply qfa-theorem there and eliminate inversion by its unique ring-definable graph. The resulting parameter-free ring sentence characterizes K among finitely generated fields.
items.locator: §5 final sentence, explicit bridge to AKNS Proposition 2.28
items.note: Authored proof bridge making the source's compressed final implication valid; no claim that an infinite field is finitely generated as a ring.
proofSteps: Expand by a total inverse symbol defined uniquely by (x=0 and y=0) or xy=1.
Field generation becomes structure generation in this finite language.
Transfer bi-interpretability through the definitional expansion, apply QFA, then eliminate the inverse symbol.

items.name: Discreteness of one-variable valuation rings
items.statement: Let k and F be fields with k→F and IsFunctionField k F. Every proper valuation subring A⊊F containing the image of k is a discrete valuation ring.
items.locator: Proposition 3.10, last step; pinned OfValuationSubring.lean, theorem at line 217
proofSteps: Apply the existing function-field theorem; no perfectness or separability assumption is required.

items.name: Places recover their valuation rings
items.statement: Under the preceding hypotheses there is a unique place P of F/k whose ring of integers is A.
items.locator: Notations 4.1 and Theorem 4.2, curve/place dictionary; pinned OfValuationSubring.lean lines 289–339
proofSteps: Use Place.ofValuationSubring and its integers equality; uniqueness is integers_injective.

items.name: Regular projective model of a one-variable field
items.statement: For a finitely generated extension F/k of transcendence degree one, normalization of P¹_k in F gives a regular projective integral k-curve with function field F and closed points corresponding to the places of F/k. Over imperfect k, do not replace regular by smooth without additional assumptions.
proofSteps: Import upstream AlgebraicCurves Layer 12B–D and its point/place order dictionary.

items.name: Finiteness of normalization over arithmetic polynomial rings
items.statement: Let A be a field or the ring of integers of a number field, T a finite tuple of independent variables, and E/Frac(A[T]) a finite field extension. The integral closure of A[T] in E is a finite A[T]-module, without a separability restriction.
items.note: Same existing A0-extension owner. The reviewed audit already identifies the purely inseparable polynomial result; this continuation imports it explicitly. General excellent-scheme normalization is a different, broader target.
proofSteps: For characteristic-zero A (a field or a number-field integer ring), A[T] is normal noetherian and every finite fraction-field extension is separable: invoke IsIntegralClosure.finite.
For a field k of positive characteristic, put P=k[T] and enlarge E/Frac(P) to its finite normal envelope N.
Let I=N^Aut(N/Frac(P)). Import the purely inseparable lower step Frac(P)⊂I and the Galois upper step I⊂N. The reverse ordering is essential.
The integral closure C of P in I is finite over P by the pinned purely inseparable polynomial theorem. C is normal noetherian with fraction field I.
Apply the pinned separable theorem to C⊂N; transfer the resulting integral closure down to P using tower_bot and transitivity of module finiteness.

Descend to E using the pinned injective finite-normalization theorem. Only the assembly, normal/noetherian polynomial instances and algebra/fraction-field tower adapters remain; a new general excellence theory is unnecessary for this consumer.

items.name: Existing separable finite-normalization theorem
items.statement: Let A be an integrally closed noetherian domain, K its fraction field, L/K a finite separable extension, and C an integral closure of A in L with compatible algebra structures. Then C is a finite A-module.
items.locator: Proposition 5.1 input, separable special case; Mathlib DedekindDomain/IntegralClosure.lean
proofSteps: Invoke IsIntegralClosure.finite with the fraction-field and scalar-tower instances.

items.name: Normal noetherian domains are intersections of height-one localizations
items.statement: For a normal noetherian integral domain A with fraction field F, A equals the intersection inside F of A_p over height-one primes p. Those localizations are DVRs; for a field A the empty intersection is F=A.
items.note: The reviewed AUDIT-23 target at L4 explicitly plans the general normal-noetherian height-one descent. Import its early commutative-algebra theorem, not the later automorphic conclusions. Removed from the A0-extension route to avoid duplicate ownership.
proofSteps: Write x=b/a in Frac(A), a≠0. If x lies in every height-one localization, b mod a vanishes at each associated prime of A/aA by principal-associated-height-one.
Associated-localization-detection gives b∈aA, hence x∈A. The reverse inclusion is immediate.
At a height-one prime, localization is a noetherian normal local domain with a unique nonzero prime; import normal-local-dvr. If A is a field the intersection is empty and is Frac(A)=A.

items.name: Roundness of quadratic Pfister forms
items.statement: For every quadratic Pfister form in either characteristic, its nonzero represented values form its similarity-factor group. Tensoring a regular round quadratic form by a binary bilinear Pfister factor preserves roundness.
items.locator: EKM Proposition 9.8(1), Corollary 9.9; input to Fact 3.1
proofSteps: Write a represented value as x−ay and, when both terms are nonzero, absorb x and y by similarity.
Induct on the number of factors; the norm binary form supplies the base case.

items.name: Arason–Pfister dimension bound
items.statement: For every field F and n>=1, a nonzero anisotropic nonsingular quadratic form with Witt class in I_q^n(F) has dimension at least 2^n, where I_q^n=I(F)^{n−1} I_q(F).
proofSteps: Write the class as a sum of scaled n-fold Pfister forms and induct on the number of summands.
Pass to the function field of the last Pfister quadric. If the form becomes hyperbolic, use the subform theorem; otherwise apply induction to its anisotropic part.
The subform theorem and Witt cancellation are imported proof leaves, not proved by this extraction.

items.name: Graded quadratic Witt invariant
items.statement: For n>=1 over every field F, the invariant e_n:I_q^n(F)→H^n(F,Z/2(n−1)) is surjective with kernel I_q^{n+1}(F), and agrees on n-fold Pfister forms with the symbol invariant. In characteristic two this uses Kato's quadratic/logarithmic comparison.
proofSteps: Away from characteristic two combine the graded Witt/Milnor-K comparison with the norm-residue theorem imported from MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.5d.
In characteristic two use Kato's theorem with logarithmic coefficients supplied by CrystallineCohomology:CR.4 and HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory:HL.2.
EKM states the general theorem as a fact with original references; their full proofs are not audited here.

items.name: Completely split places outside a finite set
items.statement: For a finite separable extension l/k of global fields and a finite set Σ of places of k, there is a finite place outside Σ splitting completely in l; in fact infinitely many such places exist.
items.locator: Lemma 3.5, first and second choices of places
items.note: Use the identity Frobenius class in the Galois closure. These already-owned prime-distribution theorems are imports, not re-planned in the Dittmann–Pop extension.
proofSteps: Pass to the Galois closure and apply the completely split case of the global Chebotarev theorem, treating the constant-field extension in the function-field case.
