Import global prime-distribution ownership; original theorem matching remains a gap, not a new proof claim.

items.name: Global approximation with one exceptional pole
items.statement: For a global field k, finite nonempty prescribed set S of places, local open conditions at S, and an auxiliary finite place v0 outside S, choose an element satisfying those conditions and integral at every finite place outside S∪{v0}.
items.note: Function-field branch is already available. Only the number-field off-a-finite-place variant and its local-open adapters remain for ownership/signature audit; do not rebuild the function-field theorem or upstream weak approximation.
proofSteps: Use strong approximation off v0 after arranging the local norm and valuation conditions are nonempty opens.
Weak approximation supplies the earlier choice of a0.

items.name: Henselian generator with simple reduction
items.statement: If a finite extension E/F embeds in the henselization of (F,w), choose a primitive generator η which is a valuation unit and whose monic minimal polynomial has integral coefficients and unit derivative at η. Then there is x∈F with w(x−η)>0.
proofSteps: Use the CRT residue-one generator η and its simple minimal polynomial; this is the residue-degree-one specialization of the fully read Kuhlmann–Novacoski Theorem 1.2 proof.
Take x=1, since w(η−1)>0. The more general residue approximation follows from immediacy.

items.name: Étale specialization and Laurent-series embedding
items.statement: Let l/k(t_2,…,t_{d−1}) be finite separable. After restricting a dense open of the torus, its normalization is finite étale; at a point ε∈(k×)^{d−2} in that open, each point above ε has finite separable residue k_ε/k and completed local ring k_ε[[t_2−ε_2,…,t_{d−1}−ε_{d−1}]]. Consequently l embeds into the iterated Laurent-series field in those parameters.
proofSteps: Use finite normalization for the field-base polynomial ring, then generic separability of the finite map.
Remove the non-étale locus, use formal étaleness to identify the completion, then embed its fraction field in iterated Laurent series.
Record the extension of the generic normalization input from A to a global field explicitly; do not use the arithmetic polynomial statement alone.

items.name: Integral closure detected by prolonged valuation rings
items.statement: Let E/F be a finite field extension and B an intersection of valuation rings O_v in F. The integral closure of B in E equals the intersection of every valuation ring of E prolonging one of these v.
items.note: The empty selected family gives B=F and intersection E, consistent with finite algebraicity. No assumption Frac(B)=F is needed. All prolongations are essential; preserve the split-prime negative example in the report.
proofSteps: Integral over B implies integral over every selected O_v and hence membership in every prolonged valuation ring, which is integrally closed.

For the converse fix a selected v and prolong it to a finite normal envelope of E/F. Every F-embedding of E into that envelope pulls the prolongation back to one of the quantified prolongations on E, so every conjugate of x has nonnegative valuation.

Write the monic minimal polynomial as the product of its conjugate roots WITH their inseparable multiplicities. Its coefficients belong to the prolonged valuation ring as sums of products of elements of that ring. They also belong to F, so exact contraction puts them in O_v.

Intersect the minimal-polynomial coefficient bounds over the chosen v; all coefficients lie in B and the monic equation proves integrality. Exact prolongation and coefficient descent are now separate items with proofs; their Lean adapters remain unimplemented.

items.name: Uniform global-field prime and integer predicates
items.statement: In global fields, the relevant finite-prime valuation rings form a uniformly ring-definable family; in number fields their intersection is the ring of integers and is uniformly definable. Interpret the same formulas in finite residue-number-field quotients.
items.locator: Proposition 5.1 after Fact 5.2; Rumely Introduction I–III; Poonen Theorem 2.2
proofSteps: Use the source-scoped global-field formulas, with their parameter domains and the number-field/global-function-field cases separated.
Original Rumely formula and proof audit remains open.

items.name: The dimensions one and two base cases
items.statement: Every infinite finitely generated field of Kronecker dimension at most two is parametrically bi-interpretable with Z, without a resolution-of-singularities assumption.
items.note: Explicit low-dimensional implementation adapter using Remark 4.4 and Rumely for number fields. Independent review rejects E18 as a new mathematical error: the required inputs are supplied by the text.
proofSteps: Use Rumely/Pop for the requisite low-dimensional valuation predicates and repeat the definable-normalization construction; the dimension-one number-field case uses its definable integer ring directly.
This extraction does not claim a completed original-source audit of these base cases.

items.name: Independent prescribed function-field orders
items.statement: For fields k⊂F, any finite set of distinct places of F/k and integers r_P admit a nonzero g∈F with ord_P(g)=r_P at every chosen place.
items.note: Actual pinned statement read; additive infinity conventions require the indicated bridge from library multiplicative valuations.
proofSteps: Apply the cited existing theorem with distinct places and the prescribed targets.

items.name: Function-field strong approximation
items.statement: For IsFunctionField k F with k relatively algebraically closed in F, a proper set S of places, finite s⊆S, targets f_P and integer precisions r_P admit x∈F satisfying v_P(x−f_P)≤exp(−r_P) for P∈s and x∈O_P for P∈S\s. The multiplicative inequality includes exact hits.
items.note: Actual pinned statement read; additive infinity conventions require the indicated bridge from library multiplicative valuations.
proofSteps: Apply the cited existing theorem with distinct places and the prescribed targets.

items.name: Existing finite polynomial normalization in a purely inseparable extension
items.statement: Let k be any field, P=k[X_i : i∈I] for finite I, K=Frac(P), and M/K a finite purely inseparable extension. With compatible algebra maps, any integral closure C of P in M is finite as a P-module. No perfectness assumption on k is required.
proofSteps: Import the pinned theorem with all fraction-field and scalar-tower instances; its proof uses a bounded Frobenius exponent and a finite coefficient-root extension.

items.name: Existing finite normal envelope
items.statement: A finite field extension E/F embeds in a finite normal extension N/F: take its normal closure inside an algebraic closure of E, with the induced compatible F- and E-algebra structures.
proofSteps: Use the normal-closure algebra map for the embedding, the normal instance in the ambient algebraically closed field, and the finite-dimensional instance.

items.name: Existing purely inseparable fixed-field step
items.statement: For a normal algebraic extension N/F, the intermediate field N^Aut(N/F) is purely inseparable over F. Finiteness of N/F is not needed for this assertion.
proofSteps: Import the pinned theorem; its proof makes every separable element fixed by all automorphisms have minimal polynomial of degree one.

items.name: Existing Galois extension over a finite-action fixed field
items.statement: If a finite group G acts on a field N by semiring automorphisms, N/FixedPoints.subfield(G,N) is Galois. Applied to G=Aut(N/F) for finite N/F, this supplies the separable upper step over N^Aut(N/F).
proofSteps: Use IsGalois.of_fixed_field; the IntermediateField fixedField carrier is compatible as demonstrated at Galois/Basic.lean:481–485.

items.name: Existing transfer of integral closure down an integral base extension
items.statement: For compatible commutative-ring maps R→A→B and C→B, if A is integral over R and C is an integral closure of A in B, then C is also an integral closure of R in B.
proofSteps: Import tower_bot, using transitivity of integrality in one direction and extension of the base in the other.

items.name: Existing descent of finite normalization through an injection
items.statement: Let A be noetherian, C its integral closure in an A-algebra M, and C′ its integral closure in another A-algebra N. If C′ is finite over A and there is an injective A-algebra map M→N, then C is finite over A. Fields and separability are not required by this declaration.
proofSteps: Lift the injection to integral closures and use noetherian finite-module descent, as in the pinned theorem.

items.name: Existing valuative criterion for integrality
items.statement: For any commutative ring R, subring B and x∈R, if every valuative relation v on R bounded by one on B also has v(x)≤v(1), then x is integral over B. The quantifier is over ALL such valuative relations.
proofSteps: Invoke the pinned arbitrary-ring theorem. Do not substitute one chosen prolongation of each selected base valuation for its universal quantifier.

items.name: Existing minimal-polynomial comparison over a normal domain
items.statement: Let R be an integrally closed domain, K=Frac(R), S a domain with compatible R- and K-algebra structures, and s∈S integral over R. Then minpoly K s is the coefficientwise image of minpoly R s. In particular its coefficients lie in R.
proofSteps: Import the primed comparison for a K-algebra S. This theorem requires integrality of s; it does not prove integrality from selected valuation bounds.

items.name: Finite conjugate-prime data for a henselian subextension
items.statement: Let (F,w) be any valued field, fix a prolongation to F^sep, and let E/F be finite inside F_w. If A=O_w and C is its integral closure in E, the maximal ideals of C over m_A form a finite family of distinct pairwise comaximal ideals. The chosen p has C_p=O_{w|E} and C/p=κ(w). Among F-embeddings of E into a finite Galois hull, the identity is the unique one inducing the chosen prolongation; each other embedding induces a prime different from the chosen p. Different nonidentity embeddings need not induce pairwise different primes.
items.locator: Kuhlmann–Novacoski setting(1), Definition 3.1, Lemmas 2.5,3.2 specialized to E⊂F_w
proofSteps: Use henselization as the decomposition field: its decomposition group fixes E pointwise.
Conjugacy of primes in the finite normal hull and the decomposition-group cosets give the finite embedding/prime correspondence.

Localization of the integral closure at the chosen prime gives the prolonged valuation ring; immediacy identifies its residue with κ(w). These valuation/Galois background interfaces still require implementation and source completion.

items.name: CRT element with residue one at the chosen prime
items.statement: In henselian-prime-orbit, there exists η∈C congruent to 1 modulo p and to 0 modulo each other maximal ideal of C over m_A. Thus η is a unit in C_p, and every nonidentity F-embedding σ of E has σ(η) reducing to zero at the fixed prolongation to a Galois hull.
items.locator: Kuhlmann–Novacoski proof of Theorem 1.2, p.11, residue-degree-one specialization
proofSteps: Apply the finite Chinese remainder theorem to the distinct maximal ideals with residues 1,0,…,0.
Translate membership in the prime induced by σ into positive valuation of σ(η). No finite-generation claim for C_p as an A-algebra is used.

items.name: Primitivity of the CRT henselian element
items.statement: The η constructed by henselian-crt-generator generates E/F. Indeed no nonidentity F-embedding of E into a normal hull fixes η, so [F(η):F]=[E:F] by separability.
proofSteps: The identity conjugate has residue 1, whereas every other embedding sends η to residue 0.

Since E/F is separable, counting embeddings extending an embedding of F(η) gives the degree equality. The identity embedding is excluded from the nonfixing claim; the source index range includes it accidentally.

items.name: Simple unit root in the conjugate polynomial
items.statement: For η above and n=[E:F], its monic minimal polynomial h belongs to A[X], and its reduction at m_A is X^(n−1)(X−1). Consequently h(η)=0, w(η)=w(h′(η))=0, w(h(1))>0 and w(h′(1))=0. The assertions include n=1 and h(1)=0, with w(0)=∞.
items.locator: Kuhlmann–Novacoski Lemma 3.3(i), pp.10–11; Theorem 1.2, specialized to residue degree one
proofSteps: Integrality of η and normality of the valuation ring give h∈A[X] using the pinned minimal-polynomial comparison.
Over a Galois hull h is the product over the distinct embeddings; CRT makes exactly one root reduce to 1 and all others to 0.
The derivative of X^(n−1)(X−1) at 1 equals 1 in every characteristic.

items.name: Finite clopen inequalities giving henselian embeddability
items.statement: For a finite E/F embedded in F_w, choose h from henselian-simple-reduction. The set of valuations v with v(a_i)≥0 for every coefficient a_i of h, v(h(1))>0, and v(h′(1))=0 is a patch-clopen neighborhood of w on which E embeds into F_v.
items.locator: Dittmann–Pop Lemma 3.9(1), with the residue-one generator from Kuhlmann–Novacoski
proofSteps: Each condition is a field patch-clopen membership or strict-membership predicate; only finitely many coefficients occur.
The Hensel simple-root criterion at 1 produces a root of h in F_v. Its irreducibility over F identifies F[X]/(h) with E and gives an embedding.
Using 1 avoids an unstated integrality condition on an arbitrary approximate root. For the source’s x, integrality also follows from monicity, integral coefficients and v(h(x))>0.

items.name: A local ring map factors through a dominating valuation ring
items.statement: For a commutative local ring R, field K and ring homomorphism f:R→K, there is a valuation subring V of K containing f(R) such that the induced map R→V is local. Injectivity and an algebraic field extension are not hypotheses of this declaration.
proofSteps: Reuse the pinned declaration with its actual typeclass hypotheses; no new implementation is claimed.

items.name: Valuation subrings are maximal for domination
items.statement: For a field F and valuation subring V⊂F, its associated local subring is maximal in the domination order: a local overring in F dominating V equals V.
proofSteps: Reuse the pinned declaration with its actual typeclass hypotheses; no new implementation is claimed.

items.name: Membership and composition for valuation pullbacks
items.statement: For field maps f:F→E, g:E→N and valuation subring W of N, x belongs to the pullback along g∘f exactly when g(f(x)) belongs to W; iterated pullback agrees with pullback along the composite. No extension or finiteness hypothesis is needed.
proofSteps: Reuse the pinned declaration with its actual typeclass hypotheses; no new implementation is claimed.

items.name: Integrality from preservation of a finite nonzero module
items.statement: Let A be a domain over a commutative ring R and M an A-module torsion-free over A, with compatible R-action. If a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule N of M is stable under multiplication by x∈A, then x is integral over R.
proofSteps: Reuse the pinned declaration with its actual typeclass hypotheses; no new implementation is claimed.

items.name: A nonzero module element detects an associated prime
items.statement: For a module M over a commutative noetherian ring R and nonzero x∈M, there is an associated prime P of M containing Ann_R(x). The module need not be finite.
items.note: The pinned definition uses radical annihilators; isAssociatedPrime_iff removes the radical over a noetherian base. Both declarations were read.
proofSteps: Reuse the pinned declaration with its actual typeclass hypotheses; no new implementation is claimed.

items.name: Height bound for a principal ideal
items.statement: In a commutative noetherian ring R, a prime ideal minimal over a principal ideal has height at most one.
proofSteps: Reuse the pinned declaration with its actual typeclass hypotheses; no new implementation is claimed.

items.name: Normal local dimension-one criterion for a DVR
items.statement: For a noetherian local domain R which is not a field, R is a DVR if and only if it is integrally closed and has exactly one nonzero prime ideal. This is the corresponding pair of entries in the pinned TFAE; converting a height-one localization into these hypotheses remains an adapter.
proofSteps: Reuse the pinned declaration with its actual typeclass hypotheses; no new implementation is claimed.

items.name: An associated prime localizes to an associated maximal ideal
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, R-module M and prime p associated to M in the pinned radical-annihilator convention, the maximal ideal of R_p is associated to M_p in that convention. Over a noetherian base, isAssociatedPrime_iff converts both sides to ordinary associated primes.
proofSteps: Reuse the pinned declaration with its actual typeclass hypotheses; no new implementation is claimed.

items.name: Existence of an exact valuation prolongation
items.statement: For any extension of fields E/F and valuation subring V⊂F, there exists a valuation subring W⊂E with W∩F=V, and V→W is local. Value groups may enlarge; equality means equality of valuation rings after contraction, not numerical equality of independently normalized valuations.
items.locator: Stacks 00IA; direct assembly of pinned valuation-local-factor, domination-maximal and pullback
proofSteps: Apply the local factorization theorem to V→E, obtaining a local injection V→W.
W∩F is a valuation subring of F; the map V→W∩F is local because any inverse in the smaller ring is also an inverse in W.
Maximality of V under domination forces W∩F=V. This works for arbitrary rank, the trivial valuation, and inseparable extensions.

items.name: All conjugates control the coefficients of a minimal polynomial
items.statement: Let E/F be finite, N/F a finite normal extension containing E, V⊂F a valuation ring and W⊂N an exact prolongation of V. If σ(x)∈W for every F-embedding σ:E→N, then every coefficient of the monic minimal polynomial of x over F belongs to V. Repeated roots in inseparable characteristic are counted with multiplicity.
items.locator: Lemma 5.3 valuation-intersection step; direct coefficient argument in this report
items.note: Acceptance: a split quadratic with two different valuations; a purely inseparable polynomial X^p−a with its repeated root; the trivial extension. Embedding extension and splitting APIs still need exact Lean adapters.
proofSteps: Every root of minpoly_F(x) in N is the image of x under an F-embedding E→N: extend the embedding of F(x), using normality of N/F.
Factor the polynomial into linear factors with repetitions. Its coefficients lie in W because all roots lie there and W is a subring.
The coefficients are also in F, so W∩F=V puts them in V. No separability assumption removes multiplicities.

items.name: Associated primes of a nonzero principal quotient have height one
items.statement: For a noetherian integrally closed domain A and nonzero a∈A, every associated prime of A/aA has height one. If a is a unit, the module is zero and the assertion is vacuous.
items.locator: Stacks 031T(1); direct determinant proof supplied in this continuation
items.note: Use the noetherian isAssociatedPrime_iff recorded in associated-prime-witness to pass from the pinned radical-annihilator carrier to an exact annihilator. Localization normality, quotient comparison and fraction-field coercions remain Lean adapters.
proofSteps: Localize at an associated prime p. In the normal local domain R=A_p choose b mod a with annihilator its maximal ideal m, and put x=b/a∉R. Then xm⊂R.
If xm⊂m, apply determinant-integrality to the nonzero finite R-submodule m⊂Frac(R). Normality would give x∈R, a contradiction.
Otherwise choose t∈m with xt a unit. For y∈m, y/t=(xy)/(xt)∈R; hence m=(t). Principal-height-bound gives dim R≤1, and a≠0 in p gives dim R≥1.

items.name: Associated-prime localizations detect a module element
items.statement: Over a commutative noetherian ring A, the map M→∏_{p∈Ass_A(M)} M_p is injective for any A-module M, without a finite-generation hypothesis on M.
items.locator: Stacks 0311, full proof read; pinned associated-prime witness supplies the nonzero test
proofSteps: For a nonzero x choose p∈Ass(M) with Ann(x)⊂p.
If x vanished in M_p, some s∉p would annihilate x, contradicting Ann(x)⊂p. Thus a nonzero element cannot vanish at every associated-prime localization.

items.name: A coefficient field in a henselian equicharacteristic-zero valuation ring
items.statement: Let V be a henselian valuation ring of equicharacteristic zero, F=Frac(V), and κ=V/m. There exists a subfield E⊂V on which reduction is an isomorphism E≃κ. This E is relatively algebraically closed in F.
items.locator: Proposition 3.2(3), Case 2, p.7; Milne LEC, Lemma 15.3 and proof, p.106
items.note: No completeness, rank-one or finitely generated residue-field assumption. Milne proves existence for a henselian local ring with separable residue over a contained field; the final relative-algebraic-closure assertion here uses the valuation-ring hypothesis.
proofSteps: Lift a transcendence basis of κ/Q. Every nonzero rational function in the lifts has nonzero residue, so the generated field lies in V.
Take a maximal such subfield. Any missing residue element is separable algebraic; lift its minimal polynomial and use Hensel to lift its simple root, contradicting maximality.

If z∈F is algebraic over E and z≠0, its valuation is zero: in a polynomial relation a positive or negative value would yield a unique term of least value. Reduce z, lift its residue to e∈E, and apply the same observation to z−e; positivity forces z=e.

items.name: Cohomological dimension over nonreal local constants
items.statement: Let k be a number field, v a finite or complex place, and k_v its henselization at a finite place or algebraic closure at a complex place. If L/k_v is finitely generated of transcendence degree n, then cd_2(L)≤n+2. At a complex place the sharper bound is n. In particular, L=E′k_v in Proposition 3.2(3) has cd_2(L)≤dim(E′)+1.
items.locator: Proposition 3.2(3), p.7 Claim, corrected nonreal-place step; Milne LEC Theorem 15.2, p.105
items.note: The transcendence-degree statement was read in Milne, whose proof refers to Shatz rather than supplying the full induction. Exact local-field and henselization comparison proofs remain in DP23-G3. This is a corrected planned proof input, not a newly verified proof of those general theorems.
proofSteps: Use the finite-local-field bound cd_2(k_v)=2 and its henselization/completion comparison; at a complex place k_v is algebraically closed.
Apply the transcendence-degree inequality cd_2(L)≤cd_2(k_v)+n.
Do not insert cd_2(E′) between these quantities: a formally real E′ has infinite 2-cohomological dimension.

items.name: A unique dominant valuation survives a finite sum
items.statement: For a valuation v:R→Γ₀ on a ring, a finite sum and an index j in its support, if v(f_i)<v(f_j) for every other index, then v(Σf_i)=v(f_j). In the paper’s additive convention, the unique least valuation survives. In particular a sum with a unique least finite additive valuation is nonzero.
items.locator: §1 p.2 and Proposition 3.2(3) p.7 of arXiv2012.01307v2; direct proof refinement supplied in this continuation
items.note: A mathematical proof interface; no Lean implementation claimed.
proofSteps: Read Valuation.map_sum_eq_of_lt at the pinned Mathlib, including j∈s and strict domination of all remaining summands. Translate multiplicative maximum to additive minimum.

items.name: A field generated by finitely many algebraic elements is finite
items.statement: For fields F⊂E and a finite set S⊂E whose elements are algebraic over F, the intermediate field F(S) is finite-dimensional over F. No separability hypothesis is required.
items.locator: §1 p.2 and Proposition 3.2(3) p.7 of arXiv2012.01307v2; direct proof refinement supplied in this continuation
items.note: A mathematical proof interface; no Lean implementation claimed.
proofSteps: Read IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_adjoin. Its IsIntegral hypotheses are equivalent to algebraicity over a field. Apply to a finite field-generating set after identifying the rational subfield in the two constructions below.

items.name: A nontrivial cyclic value group gives a DVR
items.statement: For a field valuation v with nontrivial cyclic actual value group, the valuation subring is a discrete valuation ring. The hypothesis is on the actual value group of v, not an ambient ordered group which may contain unused directions.
items.locator: §1 p.2 and Proposition 3.2(3) p.7 of arXiv2012.01307v2; direct proof refinement supplied in this continuation
items.note: A mathematical proof interface; no Lean implementation claimed.
proofSteps: Read Valuation.IsRankOneDiscrete.mk′ and Valuation.valuationSubring_isDiscreteValuationRing at the pin with their IsCyclic and Nontrivial valueGroup binders.

items.name: Restriction of a field valuation to the prime field
items.statement: Let v be any field valuation, written additively on nonzero elements, with residue field κ_v. If F and κ_v have the same characteristic, v is trivial on the prime field. If char F=0 and char κ_v=p>0, then v(p)>0 and v(q)=ord_p(q)·v(p) for every nonzero q∈Q. No rank, discreteness or henselianity hypothesis is imposed.
items.locator: §1 p.2 and Proposition 3.2(3) p.7 of arXiv2012.01307v2; direct proof refinement supplied in this continuation
items.note: A mathematical proof interface; no Lean implementation claimed.
proofSteps: The image of Z lies in the valuation ring because v(1)=0 and the valuation inequality gives v(n)≥0. Its reduction kernel is (p) when the residue characteristic is p, and zero in characteristic zero.
A nonzero integer whose residue is nonzero is a unit of the valuation ring. Hence in mixed characteristic only p contributes, and writing a rational number as p^m*a/b with p∤ab gives the formula.

In positive equal characteristic, the nonzero prime-field elements form a finite multiplicative group. An ordered value group is torsion-free, so their valuations vanish. In characteristic zero with characteristic-zero residue, every nonzero rational has valuation zero.

items.name: Algebraically independent residues lift to a unit subfield
items.statement: Suppose v is trivial on a subfield k⊂F, so k embeds in the residue field. If units x_1,…,x_s have residues algebraically independent over k, then x is algebraically independent over k, v is trivial on k(x), and the residue map identifies k(x) with k(x̄). If t∈F has v(t)>0, the tuple(x,t) is algebraically independent over k.
items.locator: §1 p.2 and Proposition 3.2(3) p.7 of arXiv2012.01307v2; direct proof refinement supplied in this continuation
items.note: A mathematical proof interface; no Lean implementation claimed.
proofSteps: For a nonzero polynomial P over k, reduction of P(x) is P(x̄)≠0. Thus P(x) is a unit and cannot vanish. Ratios give the field and residue identifications.
For a nonzero polynomial Σ_j P_j(x)t^j, each nonzero coefficient P_j(x) has value 0, so the nonzero summands have distinct values j*v(t). The unique least value survives by dominant-valuation-sum.
This argument holds for every finite residue-independent tuple, even when the residue field is not finitely generated.

items.name: A one-variable valued subfield in the geometric case
items.statement: Let K be finitely generated over its prime field k, let v be a nontrivial valuation with char Kv=char K, and suppose trdeg_k Kv=trdeg_k K−1=s. Lift a residue transcendence basis x̄ of length s to units x and choose t with v(t)>0. Then F0=k(x,t)⊂K has K/F0 finite, vF0=Z*v(t) and residue field k(x̄). Equivalently, K is a one-variable algebraic function field over k(x), and its valuation ring is proper and contains k(x).
items.locator: §1 p.2 and Proposition 3.2(3) p.7 of arXiv2012.01307v2; direct proof refinement supplied in this continuation
items.note: A mathematical proof interface; no Lean implementation claimed.
proofSteps: The residue-dimension assumption ensures s≥0 and trdeg_k K=s+1. Nontriviality permits choosing t of positive value, replacing an element by its inverse if needed.
The preceding lifting lemma makes(x,t) a transcendence basis of K/k. Because K is finitely generated as a field, it is finite over F0 by finite-algebraic-adjoin.
A polynomial in t with coefficients in k(x) has valuation equal to its least nonzero exponent times v(t). For a rational function, subtract the least exponents of numerator and denominator.

For a value-zero rational function, cancel the common t-power; its residue is the ratio of the two nonzero constant coefficients in k(x̄). This proves the full value-group and residue-field statements.
The alternative one-variable description lets the existing function-field-discreteness theorem prove the DVR assertion directly; it is an import, not another proof of that library theorem.

items.name: A Gauss valued rational subfield above a prime
items.statement: Let K be finitely generated over Q, let v have residue characteristic p>0 and suppose trdeg_Fp Kv=trdeg_Q K=s. Lift a residue transcendence basis x̄ of length s to units x. Then F0=Q(x)⊂K has K/F0 finite, vF0=Z*v(p) and residue field Fp(x̄). For every nonzero polynomial P∈Q[X], v(P(x))=min_a ord_p(P_a)*v(p), the minimum taken over nonzero coefficients.
items.locator: §1 p.2 and Proposition 3.2(3) p.7 of arXiv2012.01307v2; direct proof refinement supplied in this continuation
items.note: A mathematical proof interface; no Lean implementation claimed.
proofSteps: Let m be the least p-adic order of a nonzero coefficient of P. Multiplying by p^−m gives coefficients integral at p and a nonzero reduction polynomial.
Algebraic independence of x̄ makes this polynomial nonzero after residue evaluation. The scaled value is 0, proving the stated Gauss formula and algebraic independence of x over Q.
The equality of transcendence degrees makes K algebraic over Q(x); finite field generation and finite-algebraic-adjoin make the extension finite.

For fractions subtract the two Gauss values. A value-zero ratio can be scaled to a ratio of polynomials with coefficient minimum 0, whose residue is the ratio of their nonzero reductions. This identifies the residue field with Fp(x̄), not just a subfield of it.
For s=0 this is the usual p-adic valuation on Q. Nothing requires henselianity or completion, and the initial valuation on K need not have rank one.

items.name: The fundamental inequality for one arbitrary valuation extension
items.statement: For a finite field extension E/F with a valuation w on E and its restriction v to F, let Γ_F⊂Γ_E be their actual value groups and κ_F⊂κ_E their residue fields. Then e=[Γ_E:Γ_F] and f=[κ_E:κ_F] are finite and e*f≤[E:F]. No discreteness, rank-one, henselianity or separability assumption is needed.
items.locator: §1 p.2 and Proposition 3.2(3) p.7 of arXiv2012.01307v2; direct proof refinement supplied in this continuation
items.note: A mathematical proof interface; no Lean implementation claimed.
proofSteps: Choose a finite family u_i∈E× whose values lie in pairwise distinct cosets modulo Γ_F, and a finite family of units y_j whose residues are κ_F-linearly independent.

In a putative relation Σ_i,j a_ij*u_i*y_j=0, consider each nonzero coefficient block A_i=Σ_j a_ij*y_j. Choose a coefficient a_i0 of least value and divide the block by it. All resulting coefficients are v-integral, at least one has nonzero residue, and residue independence implies the reduced combination is nonzero. Thus A_i≠0 and w(A_i)=v(a_i0)∈Γ_F.
The nonzero terms u_i*A_i have pairwise distinct values, since their cosets are distinct. A unique least-valued term cannot cancel. Therefore the products u_i*y_j are F-linearly independent.

If N=[E:F], taking one residue vector bounds every finite family of value cosets by N, so there are at most N cosets. Taking one value coset bounds all finite residue-independent families by N, so the residue extension is finite-dimensional.

Now choose all e cosets and a residue basis of size f. The same independence argument gives e*f≤N. This directly proves the required arbitrary-valued input; the pinned TauCeti.Place inequality assumes discrete function-field places and is not used circularly.

items.name: A finite-index cyclic subgroup forces an ordered value group to be cyclic
items.statement: Let Γ be a linearly ordered abelian group and β>0. If the subgroup Zβ has finite index e in Γ, then Γ is nontrivial cyclic and order-isomorphic to Z. In particular a valuation extending a discrete valuation across a finite field extension has a nontrivial cyclic actual value group, by valuation-extension-ef.
items.locator: §1 p.2 and Proposition 3.2(3) p.7 of arXiv2012.01307v2; direct proof refinement supplied in this continuation
items.note: A mathematical proof interface; no Lean implementation claimed.
proofSteps: The finite quotient Γ/Zβ has order e, so for every γ∈Γ there is a unique integer n with eγ=nβ. Uniqueness uses β≠0 and torsion-freeness of an ordered group.
The assignment γ↦n is an additive order-preserving injection into Z: multiplication by the positive integer e and by β preserve and reflect order.
Its image is a nonzero subgroup of Z, hence cyclic with a least positive generator. Transport that generator back to Γ.
When both valuations are normalized to Z, restriction multiplies by the index e. Equality of valuation rings under restriction does not mean equality of independently normalized numerical valuations.

items.name: First-order expressibility of niceness and the test-form unit condition
items.statement: There is a ring formula ν(a_1, a_0, ε, z), uniform over all fields K satisfying (H_d) for fixed d, such that whenever the parameters z define a relatively algebraically closed global subfield k_1 ⊂ K (global-subfield-definability), K ⊨ ν(a_1, a_0, ε, z) holds exactly when a_1, a_0, ε_i ∈ k_1^×, the Pfister form q_{a_1,a_0} is k_1-nice (Definition 3.3), and every ε_i is a v-unit at every finite place v of k_1 with v(a_1) > 0 (Notations/Remarks 4.1(1)(c)). Hence the admissible test data of Recipe 4.3(1) form a uniformly definable family.
items.locator: Notations/Remarks 4.1(1)(c), p. 14, and Recipe 4.3(1), p. 15; E17
items.note: The paper asserts that the data of Notations/Remarks 4.1 are uniformly first-order definable (Recipe 4.3(1)) but does not say why niceness is, although it quantifies over the places of k_1 (E17). The proof steps are this continuation's repair.
proofSteps: Use Rumely's uniform family of finite valuation rings of the definable global subfield k_1. A dyadic place is characterized by char(k_1)=0 AND 2 being a nonunit of O_v; characteristic-two places are not dyadic in this convention. Nonzero a is a unit iff both a and a^{-1} belong to O_v; positive value means a lies in its maximal ideal.

For each finite place and the nonsingular four-variable tail q, quantify a nonzero scalar lambda making every coefficient of Q=lambda*q integral, a primitive vector x in O_v^4, and one of the four indices j. Put g(T)=Q(x+T e_j). Require g'(0) nonzero and g(0)/(g'(0))^2 in the maximal ideal. These are finitely many ring predicates, with denominators translated by multiplication. No factor 4a_1a_0 is inverted.

The strict Hensel inequality v(g(0))>2v(g'(0)) gives a root T with v(T)>v(g'(0))>=0 in the henselization. Thus x+T e_j remains primitive and is a nonzero zero of q. Conversely normalize a nonzero isotropic vector in the henselization to be primitive; nonsingularity gives a nonzero partial derivative. Density of the global field in its rank-one henselization gives an O_v-vector approximation satisfying the strict inequality. This proves the equivalence in odd, dyadic, and equal characteristic two.

Only in characteristic zero, handle real places by the absence of an ordering with a_1<0 and a_0<0. The field preordering criterion gives -1=sigma_0-sigma_1*a_1-sigma_2*a_0+sigma_3*a_1*a_0, where each sigma_i is a sum of squares. Over a number field each is a sum of four squares, so this is a fixed finite formula. Positive characteristic has no real-place clause.

Require local isotropy at the finite places which are dyadic or have v(a_0) nonzero or v(a_1)<0, and require every epsilon_i to be a unit whenever v(a_1)>0. Quantify all variables over the definable k_1 and substitute its defining formula.

items.name: Fundamental equality for function fields in one variable, without separability
items.statement: Let K ⊇ K′ be function fields in one variable over a field k_0 with [K : K′] finite, and let w′ be a place of K′ trivial on k_0. Then Σ_{w|w′} e(w|w′) f(w|w′) = [K : K′], the sum running over the places w of K above w′. In particular, if w′ has a unique prolongation w (for instance if K|K′ is purely inseparable), then e(w|w′) f(w|w′) = [K : K′].
